title: A Memory-Efficient Adjoint State Optimization Method Based on Time-Reversible Dynamical Low-Rank Approximation
summary: The primary challenge of conducting PDE-constrained optimization for high-dimensional problems, such as kinetic equations, is the often prohibitive memory cost. Computing gradients using the adjoint state method would require the storage of the entire time history of the forward solution. For such problems, where the memory cost for storing a single instance of the forward solution can already be a limiting factor, this is clearly not feasible. In this paper, we propose a memory-efficient adjoint state method that compresses the forward and adjoint solution with a dynamical low-rank approximation (a model order reduction technique) and bypasses the need to store the entire forward solution by employing a time-reversible low-rank integrator. The dynamical low-rank approach introduces a number of challenges: reversibility can fail in the rank-deficient case and the low-rank trajectories can show chaotic behavior. In particular, the latter has a number of important consequences for the optimization problem. We address those challenges and show that our method can drastically reduce the memory requirement for gradient-based optimization of kinetic equations. In particular, we consider two examples from kinetic plasma physics: optimizing beam profiles to suppress a bump-on-tail instability and shaping a particle beam using external electric fields.

AI.tldr: A memory-efficient adjoint state method for PDE-constrained optimization of high-dimensional kinetic equations, using dynamical low-rank approximation to compress forward/adjoint solutions and a time-reversible low-rank integrator to avoid storing the entire forward solution history.
AI.motivation: PDE-constrained optimization for high-dimensional problems like kinetic equations faces prohibitive memory costs: the adjoint state method requires storing the full time history of the forward solution, which is infeasible when even a single forward solution instance already strains memory limits.
AI.method: The authors propose compressing forward and adjoint solutions using dynamical low-rank approximation (a model order reduction technique) and employing a time-reversible low-rank integrator to bypass storing the entire forward solution. They address challenges including reversibility failure in rank-deficient cases and chaotic behavior in low-rank trajectories.
AI.result: The method drastically reduces memory requirements for gradient-based optimization of kinetic equations. Demonstrated on two kinetic plasma physics examples: optimizing beam profiles to suppress bump-on-tail instability and shaping particle beams using external electric fields.
AI.conclusion: The proposed memory-efficient adjoint method successfully handles high-dimensional PDE-constrained optimization problems by mitigating the dominant memory bottleneck, despite addressing nontrivial challenges introduced by the low-rank approximation framework.

title: A Data-Driven Computational Framework for Incompressible Flow in Hydraulic Networks
summary: The classical procedure for solving hydraulic networks relies on the assumption of constitutive equations, which state the relationship between the pressure gradient and fluxes along an edge. In this paper, we propose a data-driven framework that bypasses these constitutive models, formulating the incompressible flow problem directly on the graph topology. By assigning discrete measured data points to network edges, the problem is cast as a mixed-integer quadratic optimization over nodal pressures, edgewise states, and data assignments, accommodating both laminar (convex) and turbulent (non-convex) regimes. To solve this, we evaluate three algorithms: a GPU-accelerated Brute Force method, the Alternating Direction Method (ADM), and Deterministic Annealing (DA). The Brute Force method certifies global optima for small networks, establishing a good baseline for the iterative solvers. We demonstrate that ADM is highly sensitive to its initialization, requiring a faithful surrogate model to avoid local minima. In contrast, DA eliminates this dependence through unsupervised clustering. By annealing the data assignment from the centroid to strict nearest-neighbor projections, DA consistently reaches the global optimum without prior manifold reconstruction. Furthermore, numerical experiments reveal that DA is robust to noisy data, remains thermodynamically admissible on all but the coarsest and noisiest datasets, and sustains its convergence rate on larger networks where Brute Force is intractable and ADM degrades. Finally, the framework is successfully validated on complex configurations, including mixed-component networks and a $958$-edge arteriovenous bed featuring a non-Newtonian Carreau--Yasuda model, demonstrating its scalability and practical applicability.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a data-driven framework for solving incompressible hydraulic network problems directly on graph topology, bypassing traditional constitutive equations. The problem is formulated as a mixed-integer quadratic optimization and solved via three algorithms (GPU-accelerated Brute Force, Alternating Direction Method, and Deterministic Annealing). DA consistently reaches global optima without initialization dependence, is robust to noise, and scales to large networks including a 958-edge arteriovenous bed.
AI.motivation: Classical hydraulic network solvers rely on constitutive equations relating pressure gradients to fluxes, which may be inaccurate or unknown. The authors aim to bypass these models by using discrete measured data points directly, enabling data-driven solutions without prior physical model assumptions.
AI.method: The problem is formulated as a mixed-integer quadratic optimization over nodal pressures, edgewise states, and data assignments, handling both laminar (convex) and turbulent (non-convex) regimes. Three algorithms are evaluated: GPU-accelerated Brute Force (certifies global optima for small networks), Alternating Direction Method (ADM), and Deterministic Annealing (DA) which anneals data assignment from centroid to strict nearest-neighbor projections for unsupervised clustering.
AI.result: ADM is highly initialization-sensitive and requires a faithful surrogate model. DA eliminates this dependence, consistently reaching global optima without prior manifold reconstruction. DA is robust to noise, thermodynamically admissible on all but coarsest/noisiest datasets, and maintains convergence on large networks where Brute Force is intractable and ADM degrades. Validated on mixed-component networks and a 958-edge arteriovenous bed with non-Newtonian Carreau-Yasuda model.
AI.conclusion: The deterministic annealing approach provides a scalable, robust, and initialization-independent data-driven solver for hydraulic networks that bypasses constitutive models, with demonstrated applicability to complex physiological flow networks.

title: Tensor greedy double block extended Kaczmarz method for solving inconsistent tensor linear systems under t-product
summary: The randomized extended Kaczmarz method is an effective iterative framework for solving large-scale inconsistent linear systems. In this paper, we extend this framework to third-order inconsistent tensor linear systems under the t-product and propose the Tensor Greedy Double Block Extended Kaczmarz (TGDBEK) method. At each iteration, TGDBEK dynamically constructs active blocks of row and column slices via a residual-based greedy selection strategy, prioritizing the slices associated with the largest residual norms. Unlike existing tensor block Kaczmarz variants that rely on static, predefined partitions -- the tensor randomized extended block Kaczmarz (TREBK) method, its greedy counterpart (TREGBK), and the tensor randomized extended average block Kaczmarz (TREABK) method -- TGDBEK adapts the active block sizes dynamically at each step using a single intuitive threshold parameter $η$. We establish the theoretical linear convergence of TGDBEK to the unique minimum-norm least-squares solution $\mathcal{A}^\dagger * \mathcal{B}$. Extensive numerical benchmarks on synthetic dense and sparse tensor systems, as well as multidimensional multichannel color and 3D volumetric MRI image deblurring problems, demonstrate that TGDBEK substantially outperforms state-of-the-art tensor Kaczmarz solvers in both iteration count and CPU running time.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the randomized extended Kaczmarz method to third-order inconsistent tensor linear systems under the t-product, proposing the Tensor Greedy Double Block Extended Kaczmarz (TGDBEK) method. TGDBEK dynamically selects active blocks of row and column slices using a residual-based greedy strategy with a single threshold parameter η, achieving linear convergence to the unique minimum-norm least-squares solution and outperforming existing tensor Kaczmarz solvers in iterations and CPU time.
AI.motivation: Existing tensor block Kaczmarz variants (TREBK, TREGBK, TREABK) rely on static, predefined partitions, which limit their adaptability and efficiency for large-scale inconsistent linear systems. The authors aim to overcome this limitation by introducing dynamic, greedy block selection.
AI.method: TGDBEK dynamically constructs active blocks of row and column slices via residual-based greedy selection, prioritizing slices with the largest residual norms. The active block size adapts at each step using a single intuitive threshold parameter η, extending the randomized extended Kaczmarz framework to third-order tensor systems under the t-product.
AI.result: Theoretical linear convergence to the unique minimum-norm least-squares solution A†*B is established. Numerical benchmarks on synthetic dense/sparse tensors and multidimensional multichannel color and 3D volumetric MRI image deblurring problems show TGDBEK substantially outperforms state-of-the-art tensor Kaczmarz solvers in iteration count and CPU running time.
AI.conclusion: TGDBEK offers a more adaptive and efficient approach to solving large-scale inconsistent tensor linear systems, with both theoretical convergence guarantees and demonstrated practical superiority over existing methods.

title: Wasserstein Moment Nudging for Vlasov-Poisson Data Assimilation
summary: We introduce a continuous data assimilation method for particle-in-cell simulations of the Vlasov-Poisson equation when only hydrodynamic moments are observed. The forecast state is an empirical measure on phase space, whereas the observed fields (density, bulk velocity, and temperature) constrain only a few velocity moments and leave the velocity-space shape of the distribution undetermined. We construct the moment feedback as a Wasserstein gradient flow of a moment-mismatch functional over phase-space measures. The resulting drift acts directly on particle positions and velocities, couples the density, momentum, and energy residuals through a single variational structure, and vanishes on the entire moment-compatible set. Under the standard Wasserstein metric, the energy residual produces a position correction that grows quadratically with the particle speed, and the particle system falls outside standard well-posedness theory. Our primary formulation pairs the quadratic moment mismatch with a velocity-weighted Wasserstein metric that penalizes spatial transport at large peculiar velocity relative to the observed bulk flow, which removes this growth. A direction-split variant retains the plain metric instead. Under the same weighted metric, an alternative moment-relative-entropy functional yields an affine, shape-preserving velocity correction and explicit global moment balances for the space-inhomogeneous system. We prove that the finite-particle scheme with linear Lenard-Bernstein collisions is globally well posed. In 1D1V and 2D2V experiments with several collision models, the nudged formulations reduce bulk-velocity and temperature errors by up to two orders of magnitude relative to an unassimilated run.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a continuous data assimilation method for particle-in-cell simulations of the Vlasov-Poisson equation using only hydrodynamic moment observations, formulated as a Wasserstein gradient flow with a velocity-weighted metric to ensure well-posedness.
AI.motivation: When only hydrodynamic moments (density, bulk velocity, temperature) are observed, they constrain only a few velocity moments, leaving the velocity-space distribution shape undetermined. Standard moment feedback can cause energy residual to produce position corrections that grow quadratically with particle speed, pushing the system outside standard well-posedness theory.
AI.method: The forecast state is an empirical measure on phase space. The authors construct moment feedback as a Wasserstein gradient flow of a moment-mismatch functional over phase-space measures. The primary formulation pairs quadratic moment mismatch with a velocity-weighted Wasserstein metric penalizing spatial transport at large peculiar velocity. A direction-split variant retains the plain metric. An alternative moment-relative-entropy functional yields affine, shape-preserving velocity correction.
AI.result: The finite-particle scheme with linear Lenard-Bernstein collisions is proven globally well posed. In 1D1V and 2D2V experiments with several collision models, the nudged formulations reduce bulk-velocity and temperature errors by up to two orders of magnitude relative to an unassimilated run.
AI.conclusion: The proposed nudging method effectively assimilates hydrodynamic moment observations into particle-in-cell Vlasov-Poisson simulations while maintaining well-posedness through the velocity-weighted Wasserstein metric design.

title: Inverted model selection in physics-informed neural networks: when a lower residual selects a worse solution
summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are commonly evaluated via a single aggregate residual, assuming a smaller residual indicates a better solution. Testing this directly across three constrained PDE systems, I find this assumption can systematically fail. In matched pairs of solvers differing only in whether a defining structural identity is hard-wired or penalized, the penalized variant frequently attains a lower equation residual while violating that identity by several orders of magnitude, causing the exact variant to be falsely ranked worse. Over 64 matched pairs spanning two systems, four network variants, and eight seeds, this inversion occurs in 83\% of cases (95\% Wilson CI: 72--90\%), with rates from 72\% to 94\% across systems. Testing across six architectures--MLP, cPINN, XPINN, hp-VPINN, and physics-informed DeepONet and FNO--inverts the ranking in 46 of 48 pairs, indicating that this variability is problem-dependent rather than specific to the approximator. A third, larger vorticity--streamfunction problem shows the same ordering: the residual-optimal solver violates its structural identity by over six orders above tolerance, despite a residual margin of only 9.37%. Because a scalar loss cannot expose this, I introduce a lexicographic admissibility gate spanning the structural identity, boundary trace, and a solvability integral that must vanish independently of the equation residual. All three must pass before residuals can compete. This gate catches three artifact classes but misses a fourth: a prescribed-structure prior yields fields that pass every single-run check, yet deleting the source term reveals that 97\% of the reported structure survives removal of the physics. Reference data and figures accompany the paper.

AI.tldr: This paper challenges the common assumption in PINNs that a lower aggregate equation residual indicates a better solution. Through systematic experiments across multiple constrained PDE systems, network architectures, and matched solver pairs, the author demonstrates that penalized variants frequently achieve lower residuals while violating structural identities by orders of magnitude, causing correct solutions to be falsely ranked worse. The author proposes a lexicographic admissibility gate to address this issue but finds it misses a fourth artifact class where solutions satisfy all single-run checks yet are physically vacuous.
AI.motivation: The standard practice of evaluating PINNs via a single aggregate residual assumes smaller residuals indicate better solutions. This assumption is questionable because structural constraints (mathematical identities the solution must satisfy) can be violated even when equation residuals are low. The author aims to test whether this assumption systematically fails and to develop better evaluation criteria.
AI.method: The author constructs matched pairs of solvers that differ only in whether a defining structural identity is hard-wired or penalized, and compares their aggregate residuals. Experiments span two constrained PDE systems with four network variants and eight seeds (64 pairs), six architectures (MLP, cPINN, XPINN, hp-VPINN, DeepONet, FNO), and a third larger vorticity–streamfunction problem. A lexicographic admissibility gate is introduced requiring structural identity, boundary trace, and solvability integral checks to pass before residuals compete.
AI.result: The penalized variant attains lower equation residuals while violating structural identities by several orders of magnitude in 83% of the 64 matched pairs (95% Wilson CI: 72–90%), and in 46 of 48 pairs across six architectures. A third larger problem shows residual-optimal solver violating structural identity by six orders above tolerance with only 9.37% residual margin. The proposed admissibility gate catches three artifact classes but misses a fourth where 97% of reported structure survives removal of the physics source term.
AI.conclusion: Aggregate residual alone is an unreliable metric for PINN evaluation; structural identities must be independently verified. While the lexicographic admissibility gate improves detection of artifacts, it is insufficient, as physics-vacuous solutions can still pass single-run checks. This indicates a need for more robust evaluation frameworks for PINNs.

title: Spatial and temporal analyticity of solutions to semi-linear parabolic systems with analytic nonlinearities
summary: It is shown that the solutions to a wide class of semi-linear parabolic equations with analytic (holomorphic) nonlinearity, with spatially periodic boundary conditions, are analytic in time with values in the Gevrey class of analytic functions with respect to the spatial variable.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that solutions to a broad class of semi-linear parabolic equations with analytic nonlinearities and spatially periodic boundary conditions are analytic in time, taking values in the Gevrey class of spatially analytic functions.
AI.motivation: To establish regularity (analyticity in time and space) for solutions of semi-linear parabolic equations, extending known results to a wide class of such equations with holomorphic nonlinearities.
AI.method: The paper analyzes semi-linear parabolic equations with analytic (holomorphic) nonlinearities under spatially periodic boundary conditions, and proves that the solutions are analytic in time with values in the Gevrey class of analytic functions in the spatial variable.
AI.result: It is shown that solutions to this class of equations possess simultaneous analyticity in both time and space—specifically, analyticity in time with values in the Gevrey class of spatially analytic functions.
AI.conclusion: The established regularity result applies broadly to semi-linear parabolic equations with holomorphic nonlinearities and periodic spatial domains, demonstrating strong analytic smoothing properties of the solutions.

title: AXUV synthetic diagnostic for ASDEX Upgrade and its application for SPI simulations
comment: 16 figures (some multi-panel), 2 supplementary movies. Submitted to Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion
summary: We introduce an Absolute eXtended UltraViolet (AXUV) diode-based camera forward-modelling tool to support the validation of mitigated disruption simulations and the interpretation of experimental phenomena, with applications to the ASDEX Upgrade (AUG) tokamak. AXUV diodes measure electromagnetic radiation across a wide spectral range with a significantly higher time resolution (~microseconds) than foil bolometers (~milliseconds), albeit with a non-uniform spectral responsivity. AXUV is suitable for examining fast phenomena, such as shattered pellet injection (SPI), where the radiation localisation and radiated power provide information on the deposition of pellet material. Due to the characteristics and degradation of AXUV diodes, absolute power measurements are subject to large systematic uncertainties, especially when the spectra are time-varying, as in e.g. mixed Ne/D2 SPI experiments. These challenges motivated the development of a synthetic diagnostic within the Cherab-Raysect optical modelling framework, which is applied here to four AXUV cameras in two poloidal cross-sections of AUG. The synthetic diagnostic provides a means to understand how the diodes measure radiation under SPI conditions and to connect first-principles plasma simulations with experimental measurements. The details of the synthetic diagnostic are presented, and the capabilities are illustrated with applications to AUG SPI simulations performed in JOREK. The synthetic signals generated from these simulations are compared with experimental measurements from the 2022 SPI campaign and show qualitatively similar features in many respects. Particularly good agreement was found in the time evolution of the studied high Ne-content (10%) pellet, whereas a different, low Ne-content (0.17%) case exhibited more pronounced differences, likely due to the absence of background impurities in the underlying SPI simulations.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a synthetic diagnostic tool for AXUV diode-based cameras, developed within the Cherab-Raysect framework, to support validation of mitigated disruption simulations at the ASDEX Upgrade tokamak. The tool is applied to four AXUV cameras and tested against JOREK simulations of shattered pellet injection (SPI), showing qualitatively good agreement with experimental data, particularly for high Ne-content pellets.
AI.motivation: AXUV diodes measure radiation with high temporal resolution (microseconds) but suffer from non-uniform spectral responsivity and large systematic uncertainties in absolute power measurements, especially during time-varying spectra like mixed Ne/D2 SPI experiments. This motivates the need for a synthetic diagnostic to properly interpret experimental measurements and connect them to first-principles simulations.
AI.method: A forward-modelling synthetic diagnostic is developed within the Cherab-Raysect optical modelling framework for four AXUV cameras in two poloidal cross-sections of AUG. The tool simulates how AXUV diodes measure radiation under SPI conditions and is applied to JOREK simulations of mitigated disruptions. Synthetic signals are compared with experimental measurements from the 2022 SPI campaign.
AI.result: The synthetic diagnostic produces signals showing qualitatively similar features to experimental measurements. Particularly good agreement was found for the time evolution of a high Ne-content (10%) pellet, while a low Ne-content (0.17%) case showed more pronounced differences, likely attributable to the absence of background impurities in the underlying SPI simulations.
AI.conclusion: The AXUV synthetic diagnostic provides a validated means to interpret experimental measurements, understand diode behavior under SPI conditions, and bridge first-principles plasma simulations with experimental observations at AUG.

title: Weighted Laplacian Flow: A Deterministic Particle Flow with Provable Convergence
summary: Sampling from a target probability density is a fundamental task in statistics, machine learning, and scientific computing. We introduce weighted Laplacian flow, a deterministic particle-flow method that transports samples from a tractable initial density to a target density known up to normalization. The method evolves the logarithmic density ratio between the target and the transported distribution and constructs the particle velocity by solving a weighted Poisson equation associated with the target density. This design avoids the need to choose a kernel and enables direct control of particle weights along the flow. We establish the global well-posedness of the proposed PDE system and prove that the transported density converges to the target density in both $L^\infty$ distance and Kullback-Leibler divergence. Under a sublinear forcing condition, the method achieves exact convergence in finite time. Numerical experiments on multimodal, heavy-tailed, and ten-dimensional targets demonstrate that weighted Laplacian flow can perform long-range mass transport, overcome energy barriers.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces weighted Laplacian flow, a deterministic particle-flow method for sampling from target probability densities. It evolves a logarithmic density ratio via a weighted Poisson equation, avoids kernel selection, and provides theoretical guarantees including global well-posedness, convergence in L∞ and KL divergence, and finite-time convergence under sublinear forcing conditions.
AI.motivation: Sampling from target probability densities is fundamental across statistics, ML, and scientific computing. Existing particle-flow methods often require choosing a kernel and lack direct control over particle weights, motivating a kernel-free deterministic approach with theoretical guarantees.
AI.method: The method transports samples from a tractable initial density to a target density by evolving the logarithmic density ratio and constructing particle velocity via a weighted Poisson equation tied to the target density. This avoids kernel selection and enables direct control of particle weights along the flow.
AI.result: The paper proves global well-posedness of the PDE system, convergence of the transported density to the target in both L∞ distance and KL divergence, and exact finite-time convergence under a sublinear forcing condition. Numerical experiments on multimodal, heavy-tailed, and 10-dimensional targets show successful long-range mass transport and overcoming of energy barriers.
AI.conclusion: Weighted Laplacian flow offers a principled, kernel-free deterministic sampling method with strong theoretical convergence guarantees and demonstrated effectiveness on challenging target distributions.

title: A well-balanced weakly compressible SPH formulation for free-surface flows and its GPU implementation
summary: This study proposes a well-balanced formulation of weakly compressible smoothed particle hydrodynamics (WCSPH) for free-surface flows, which preserves hydrostatic equilibrium exactly at the discrete level--a property essential for reliable long-term simulations. Although well-balanced schemes are well established for mesh-based methods, the property remains largely unaddressed in WCSPH, where the particle approximation of the pressure gradient fails to balance the gravitational force exactly. The imbalance stems from two difficulties: the nonlinearity of the pressure-gradient-over-density term, and the approximation error of gradients evaluated by particle summation. The first is resolved by introducing an auxiliary potential variable that recasts the nonlinear term as the gradient of a single scalar, which reduces to a linear function of position under hydrostatic conditions. The second is resolved by a Riemann-based gradient approximation with kernel correction, which is first-order consistent and recovers linear fields exactly. These two ingredients ensure that the discrete potential gradient balances gravitational force exactly. Widely used techniques, including $δ-$SPH, particle shifting and tensile instability control, are readily incorporated. The formulation is further extended to three dimensions and implemented on GPU with architecture-tailored optimizations. Hydrostatic tests with rectangular, triangular and Gaussian bottom topographies show that the proposed formulation attains the well-balanced property to machine precision, reducing the spurious velocity error of conventional SPH from $10^{-3}$ to the order of $10^{-13}$. More complex benchmarks confirm its robustness, accuracy and low pressure oscillation, with simulations of up to 17.53 million particles performed on a single consumer-grade GPU.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a well-balanced formulation of weakly compressible smoothed particle hydrodynamics (WCSPH) for free-surface flows that preserves hydrostatic equilibrium exactly at the discrete level, achieving machine-precision accuracy and reducing spurious velocities from 10^-3 to 10^-13.
AI.motivation: Well-balanced schemes are well established for mesh-based methods but remain largely unaddressed in WCSPH. The particle approximation of the pressure gradient fails to balance gravitational force exactly due to two difficulties: the nonlinearity of the pressure-gradient-over-density term, and the approximation error of gradients evaluated by particle summation. This imbalance is problematic for reliable long-term simulations.
AI.method: The method resolves the two sources of imbalance via: (1) introducing an auxiliary potential variable that recasts the nonlinear pressure-gradient-over-density term as the gradient of a single scalar, which becomes linear under hydrostatic conditions; and (2) using a Riemann-based gradient approximation with kernel correction that is first-order consistent and recovers linear fields exactly. The formulation incorporates widely used techniques (δ-SPH, particle shifting, tensile instability control), extends to 3D, and is implemented on GPU with tailored optimizations.
AI.result: Hydrostatic tests with rectangular, triangular, and Gaussian bottom topographies show the proposed formulation attains well-balanced property to machine precision, reducing spurious velocity error from 10^-3 to 10^-13. More complex benchmarks confirm robustness, accuracy, and low pressure oscillation, with simulations of up to 17.53 million particles on a single consumer-grade GPU.
AI.conclusion: The proposed well-balanced WCSPH formulation successfully achieves exact hydrostatic equilibrium at the discrete level, making it suitable for reliable long-term free-surface flow simulations. Its computational efficiency enables very large-scale simulations (17.53M particles) on consumer-grade GPUs.

title: On the Non-isothermal Nernst-Planck-Navier-Stokes System
summary: Electrodiffusion has been extensively studied in the isothermal setting, whereas the mathematical theory of thermally coupled electrodiffusion remains comparatively underdeveloped. We investigate a non-isothermal electrodiffusion model describing the evolution of multiple ionic species with different diffusivities and valences in a two-dimensional incompressible viscous fluid. The coupling to a spatially and temporally varying temperature gives rise to a nonlinear and nonlocal system with logarithmic nonlinearities in the ionic fluxes. We establish local well-posedness for strictly positive initial concentrations and prove global well-posedness when the initial temperature is close to a homogeneous state by developing a new entropy structure tailored to thermodiffusive effects. No smallness assumption is imposed on the initial ionic concentrations or fluid velocity. To overcome the singularity of the logarithmic terms, we develop a novel cutoff-mollification regularization, derive uniform logarithmic estimates, and prove persistence of strict positivity of the ionic concentrations. This positivity removes the singular behavior of the logarithmic nonlinearities and is essential for the uniqueness argument. These results provide a rigorous mathematical framework for the analysis of non-isothermal electrohydrodynamics systems.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes local well-posedness for a non-isothermal electrodiffusion model in 2D incompressible viscous fluids, and proves global well-posedness when initial temperature is near a homogeneous state, using a new entropy structure and a cutoff-mollification regularization to handle logarithmic singularities.
AI.motivation: While isothermal electrodiffusion is well-studied, the mathematical theory of thermally coupled electrodiffusion remains underdeveloped. This paper addresses this gap by analyzing a non-isothermal electrodiffusion model with multiple ionic species, where temperature coupling introduces nonlinear, nonlocal, and logarithmic complexities.
AI.method: The authors develop a new entropy structure tailored to thermodiffusive effects, impose no smallness assumption on ionic concentrations or fluid velocity, and use a novel cutoff-mollification regularization to overcome logarithmic singularities. They derive uniform logarithmic estimates and prove persistence of strict positivity of ionic concentrations, which removes singular behavior and enables the uniqueness argument.
AI.result: Local well-posedness is established for strictly positive initial concentrations, and global well-posedness is proven when the initial temperature is close to a homogeneous state. The strict positivity of ionic concentrations is preserved, eliminating logarithmic singularities.
AI.conclusion: These results provide a rigorous mathematical framework for analyzing non-isothermal electrohydrodynamics systems, extending the well-posedness theory from isothermal to thermally coupled electrodiffusion.

title: State-Space Model-Enabled Reinforcement Learning for Magnetic Configuration Controlon EXL-50U
summary: Accurate feedback control of the plasma current ($I_p$) and centroid position $(R_c,Z_c)$ is essential for the stable operation of spherical torus (ST) plasmas. Conventional proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controllers require extensive manual tuning and struggle with the fast, strongly coupled dynamics that arise as plasma performance improves. Reinforcement learning (RL) has recently emerged as a promising alternative to such complex magnetic control problems, yet its practical deployment on ST devices remains challenging. This paper presents a practical RL controller for the EXL-50U ST, trained within a rigid RZIP state-space model (SSM) that enables efficient offline policy learning. A lightweight plasma position reconstructor is developed to estimate $(R_c,Z_c)$ from magnetic probe signals within the real-time control cycle. The trained policy is seamlessly deployed on the EXL-50U plasma control system, achieving stable regulation of $I_p$ and $(R_c,Z_c)$ and sustaining discharges up to 650 ms under RL control. These results demonstrate the feasibility and practical potential of model-informed RL for magnetic configuration control in ST devices, offering a promising direction beyond conventional PID-based schemes.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a practical reinforcement learning (RL) controller for plasma current and centroid position control on the EXL-50U spherical torus device. The RL policy is trained offline within a rigid RZIP state-space model and deployed in real-time, achieving stable plasma regulation with discharges sustained up to 650 ms.
AI.motivation: Conventional PID controllers for plasma current and position control require extensive manual tuning and struggle with the fast, strongly coupled dynamics of spherical torus plasmas as performance improves. While RL has emerged as a promising alternative for magnetic control, practical deployment on spherical torus devices remains challenging.
AI.method: A practical RL controller is trained offline within a rigid RZIP state-space model (SSM), enabling efficient policy learning. A lightweight plasma position reconstructor estimates the centroid position from magnetic probe signals within the real-time control cycle, and the trained policy is deployed on the EXL-50U plasma control system.
AI.result: The RL controller achieves stable regulation of plasma current and centroid position, sustaining discharges up to 650 ms under RL control on the EXL-50U device.
AI.conclusion: The results demonstrate the feasibility and practical potential of model-informed RL for magnetic configuration control in spherical torus devices, offering a promising alternative direction beyond conventional PID-based schemes.

title: A diffusion time-changed stochastic SIS epidemic model: well-posedness, long-time behavior, and numerical approximation
summary: In this paper, we propose and analyze a diffusion time-changed susceptible-infected-susceptible (SIS) epidemic model driven by time-changed Brownian motion. We prove that the proposed model admits a unique global positive solution for any initial value in $(0,N)$. The extinction and persistence of the disease are then investigated. To approximate the diffusion time-changed SIS model, we construct a positivity-preserving logarithmic Euler-Maruyama (LEM) method. Assuming that the time-changed is given by the inverse of a standard $α$-stable subordinator with $α\in(0,1)$, we prove that the numerical solution converges strongly to the exact solution with order $α$. Finally, numerical experiments are provided to confirm the predicted convergence rates and illustrate the positivity-preserving property of the proposed method.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a diffusion time-changed SIS epidemic model driven by time-changed Brownian motion, proves existence of a unique global positive solution, investigates disease extinction and persistence, and develops a positivity-preserving logarithmic Euler-Maruyama method with strong convergence order α for the inverse α-stable subordinator case.
AI.motivation: To extend classical SIS epidemic models by incorporating time-changed stochastic dynamics, capturing more realistic behaviors where the underlying process is subordinated to a time-changed Brownian motion, while ensuring the numerical approximation preserves positivity of the solution.
AI.method: The paper constructs a diffusion time-changed SIS model driven by time-changed Brownian motion, proves well-posedness (unique global positive solution), analyzes extinction and persistence conditions, and designs a positivity-preserving logarithmic Euler-Maruyama (LEM) numerical scheme. Convergence analysis is performed for the case where the time-change is the inverse of a standard α-stable subordinator.
AI.result: The model admits a unique global positive solution for any initial value in (0,N). The LEM method preserves positivity and converges strongly to the exact solution with order α, where α∈(0,1) is the stability index of the subordinator. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates and positivity-preserving property.
AI.conclusion: The proposed diffusion time-changed SIS model and its positivity-preserving LEM numerical scheme are theoretically sound and practically effective, with confirmed convergence order α and preservation of solution positivity in simulations.

title: Volume-Surface-Wire Integral Equations for EEG Source Imaging
summary: In EEG source imaging, the precision of the imaging of the brain activity depends on the accuracy of the forward head model which is, in turn, affected by the representation of tissue conductivity, including anisotropic compartments such as the skull and white matter. We introduce an EEG source imaging framework based on a hybrid volume-surface-wire integral formulation, enabling tract-aware modeling of anisotropic white matter contributions without a full volumetric head discretization. The proposed framework is assessed on a realistic MRI-derived head anatomy, showing close agreement with FEM reference solutions while avoiding full-volume meshing and providing a natural representation of white matter fiber tracts. We then integrate this model into a real-time pipeline that couples EEG processing with immersive visualization, enabling synchronized inspection of scalp potentials, cortical sources, and white matter fiber tracts-related quantities. The results support the proposed formulation as a tract-aware alternative to canonical formulations, combining robust localization performance with interactive visualization capabilities.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces an EEG source imaging framework based on a hybrid volume-surface-wire integral formulation that enables tract-aware modeling of anisotropic white matter contributions without full volumetric head discretization, validated against FEM reference solutions and integrated into a real-time interactive visualization pipeline.
AI.motivation: The precision of EEG source imaging depends on the accuracy of the forward head model, which is affected by representation of tissue conductivity, particularly anisotropic compartments like the skull and white matter.
AI.method: A hybrid volume-surface-wire integral formulation is proposed for EEG source imaging, enabling tract-aware modeling of anisotropic white matter contributions without full volumetric head discretization, evaluated on a realistic MRI-derived head anatomy.
AI.result: The framework shows close agreement with FEM reference solutions while avoiding full-volume meshing, and provides a natural representation of white matter fiber tracts. It is integrated into a real-time pipeline coupling EEG processing with immersive visualization.
AI.conclusion: The proposed formulation serves as a tract-aware alternative to canonical formulations, combining robust localization performance with interactive visualization capabilities.

title: Anomalous diffusion memory factorization: Characteristic timescales and application to inverse problem
summary: Memory effects and anomalous diffusion arising in models of transport in complex media, fractals, and viscoelastic materials can be described by fractional-differential equations, such as the time-fractional diffusion equation $D^α_t u - Δ_x u = 0$. The paper develops a decomposition of solutions of these equations into a product of spatial and temporal components, corresponding to a freeze-out at long times. For fractional diffusion with the Caputo derivative the spatial factor is the inverse-Laplacian $(-Δ)^{-1}$ of the initial data, while for the Riemann-Liouville derivative it is the inverse bi-Laplacian $ (-Δ)^{-2}$. In both cases, the temporal factor of the solution is a scaled negative power of time. This memory artifact explicitly encodes the initial data, which gives a simple and robust way to reconstruct the initial conditions in the backward-in-time inverse problem with solution values measured at long times. We derive characteristic timescales for Mittag-Leffler functions, which correspond to such factorization in anomalous diffusion. This also enables an accurate approximation of the number of real zeros of the Mittag-Leffler function. We apply these results to heat transfer on a comb, a model which manifests subdiffusion arising from the comb's fractal structure.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a decomposition of solutions to fractional-diffusion equations into spatial and temporal components, where the spatial factor is an inverse Laplacian (for Caputo) or inverse bi-Laplacian (for Riemann-Liouville) of the initial data, and the temporal factor is a scaled negative power of time. This "freeze-out" behavior enables reconstruction of initial conditions from long-time measurements and provides characteristic timescales for Mittag-Leffler functions, with applications to heat transfer on combs.
AI.motivation: Fractional-diffusion equations describe transport in complex media, fractals, and viscoelastic materials, but understanding their long-time behavior and solving inverse problems (reconstructing initial conditions) remains challenging. The authors aim to exploit memory effects to develop a robust method for backward-in-time inverse problems.
AI.method: The paper decomposes solutions of time-fractional diffusion equations into product form: spatial component (inverse-Laplacian of initial data for Caputo derivative, inverse bi-Laplacian for Riemann-Liouville derivative) times a temporal component (scaled negative power of time). The authors derive characteristic timescales for Mittag-Leffler functions and use these to approximate the number of real zeros of the Mittag-Leffler function.
AI.result: The factorization explicitly encodes initial data, enabling simple and robust reconstruction of initial conditions from long-time solution values. The team derives characteristic timescales for Mittag-Leffler functions and accurate approximations of their real zero counts. The results are applied to heat transfer on a comb, a model exhibiting subdiffusion from fractal structure.
AI.conclusion: The proposed freeze-out decomposition provides a practical tool for solving backward-in-time inverse problems in fractional diffusion, with applications to fractal-structured media like combs.

title: Modified Kalman Filtering Derived from Non-Maxwellian Distribution Functions in Open Systems
summary: Kalman filtering is exact for linear dynamics with Gaussian state and observation statistics, but a mean-covariance representation cannot retain finite non-Gaussian structure generated by source-driven kinetic evolution. We formulate a modified filtering theory for open plasma systems in which the additional state structure is derived from a non-Maxwellian velocity-space distribution (NMDF) rather than introduced as an empirical residual family. A kinetic manifold defines $f_s(\mathbf X_s,\mathbf v)$, while a fixed diagnostic map $H_D$ generates the measurement PDF $p_{D,s}$; the projected kinetic equation determines the state-prediction dynamics. The posterior evolves continuously and is corrected by Bayes' rule, with positivity-constrained relative-entropy projection when required. The Gaussian posterior with affine dynamics and a linear Gaussian observation model recovers the Kalman-Bucy and discrete Kalman limits. The first explicit non-Gaussian closure is a five-coordinate INMDF from exact five-moment inversion, with Kappa retained as a broad-tail alternative. Using seven Alcator C-Mod Langmuir-probe ion-saturation-current PDFs, six kinetic manifolds are propagated through the same source statistics, noise model, normalization, and probe response. Because the published histograms lack time ordering, recursive tracking is not tested. In universal leave-one-condition-out prediction, double-INMDF ranks first in all four held-out divertor conditions, with mean error 0.0989 versus 0.1089 for MDF. Within-region calibration gives nearly identical divertor errors for first- and double-INMDF, 0.0936 and 0.0937, while two-Maxwellian gives the smallest midplane error, 0.0718. Predictions remain conditional on published source and noise controls, but show that a frozen source-to-kinetic response generalizes to an unseen current PDF and that the preferred response is region dependent.

AI.tldr: This paper formulates a modified Kalman filtering theory for open plasma systems where non-Gaussian state structure arises from a kinetic (non-Maxwellian velocity-space) manifold rather than empirical residual families. The framework generalizes Kalman-Bucy/discrete Kalman filters as special cases, introduces an explicit non-Gaussian closure (INMDF) from exact five-moment inversion, and validates it using Alcator C-Mod Langmuir-probe data, showing region-dependent generalization of frozen source-to-kinetic response.
AI.motivation: Standard Kalman filtering assumes Gaussian state statistics, but open plasma systems driven by kinetic evolution generate finite non-Gaussian structure (non-Maxwellian velocity-space distributions) that a mean-covariance representation cannot retain. The authors seek a principled filtering framework that natively incorporates this structure rather than resorting to empirical residual families.
AI.method: The authors define a kinetic manifold for the single-particle distribution f_s(X_s,v), couple it with a fixed diagnostic map H_D to generate measurement PDFs, and project the kinetic equation to determine state-prediction dynamics. Posterior evolution is continuous, corrected via Bayes' rule, with positivity-constrained relative-entropy projection. They implement an explicit five-coordinate INMDF closure via exact five-moment inversion (with Kappa as an alternative), and test six kinetic manifolds on seven Alcator C-Mod Langmuir-probe ion-saturation-current PDFs using universal leave-one-condition-out prediction.
AI.result: The Gaussian posterior with affine dynamics and linear Gaussian observations recovers Kalman-Bucy and discrete Kalman limits. In leave-one-condition-out prediction, the double-INMDF ranks first across all four held-out divertor conditions (mean error 0.0989 vs 0.1089 for MDF). Within-region calibration yields nearly identical divertor errors for first- and double-INMDF (0.0936/0.0937), while two-Maxwellian gives the smallest midplane error (0.0718), indicating the preferred kinetic response is region dependent.
AI.conclusion: A frozen source-to-kinetic response generalizes to unseen current PDFs, and the optimal kinetic manifold choice is region-dependent. However, recursive tracking could not be tested because the published histograms lack time ordering, and predictions remain conditional on published source and noise controls.

title: The Smallest Singular Value of Nonuniform Fourier Matrices
summary: We study the smallest singular value of nonuniform Fourier matrices in two settings: clustered nodes and perturbations of an equispaced grid. By reducing the problem to spectral norm estimates for periodic nonuniform interpolation matrices, we obtain nearly optimal bounds in both cases. For clustered nodes, we derive a local separation condition in which each required gap depends only on the sizes of the two neighboring clusters. For perturbations with the bound \(1/4\leq L<1/2\), our result confirms the conjecture of Austin and Trefethen on the \(2\)-norm Lebesgue constant up to a logarithmic factor.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the smallest singular value of nonuniform Fourier matrices in two settings: clustered nodes and perturbations of equispaced grids. By reducing to spectral norm estimates for periodic nonuniform interpolation matrices, the authors obtain nearly optimal bounds and confirm the Austin-Trefethen conjecture on the 2-norm Lebesgue constant up to a logarithmic factor.
AI.motivation: To understand the conditioning of nonuniform Fourier matrices, which are fundamental in signal processing, sampling theory, and numerical analysis. The smallest singular value controls the stability of reconstruction from nonuniform samples, and existing bounds were suboptimal or missing for clustered node configurations.
AI.method: The problem is reduced to spectral norm estimates for periodic nonuniform interpolation matrices. For clustered nodes, a local separation condition is derived where each required gap depends only on the sizes of the two neighboring clusters. For perturbed equispaced grids with bound 1/4 ≤ L < 1/2, the approach yields bounds on the smallest singular value.
AI.result: Nearly optimal bounds on the smallest singular value are obtained in both settings. For clustered nodes, a local separation condition is established with cluster-dependent gaps. For perturbations, the authors confirm the Austin-Trefethen conjecture on the 2-norm Lebesgue constant up to a logarithmic factor.
AI.conclusion: The reduction to interpolation matrix spectral norms provides a unified framework yielding nearly optimal conditioning estimates for nonuniform Fourier matrices in both clustered and perturbed settings, settling a conjecture up to logarithmic factors.

title: First-Principles Electron-Magnon Coupling with Machine-Learning Hamiltonians: From Band Renormalization to Transport
summary: In analogy to electron-phonon coupling (EPC), electron-magnon coupling (EMC) is expected to shape electronic structure, transport, and possibly unconventional superconductivity in magnetic materials. However, unlike EPC, which is now routinely treated within first-principles frameworks, a quantitative description of EMC, especially for transport, remains elusive because of the lack of theoretical formalism. Consequently, even for elemental iron, EPC-only calculations miss both the magnitude and the $T^2$ component of resistivity. This discrepancy has long been attributed to EMC, although direct computational evidence has been lacking and the underlying transport mechanism remains unresolved. Here we develop a unified first-principles formalism for EMC in collinear magnetic systems within many-body perturbation theory, complemented by machine-learning spinful Hamiltonians that supply quantities not directly accessible from conventional first-principles methods. Our framework enables ab initio transport calculations including EMC effects for the first time. Applied to ferromagnetic $α$-Fe, our approach yields electron spectral functions consistent with previous studies. More importantly, we recover the full $T^2$ component of resistivity with a coefficient in quantitative agreement with measurement and reveal that the $T^2$ component cannot be attributed solely to EMC, as has long been assumed, but is dominated by the strong EPC-EMC interplay. Extending to antiferromagnetic K-doped $\mathrm{BaMn_2As_2}$, our method captures the ARPES-observed magnon-induced kink and a large EMC strength of $\sim 3$ comparable to experimental measurements, demonstrating the generality of the framework. Our work closes a longstanding gap in the quantitative understanding of transport in magnetic systems and provides a predictive foundation for examining magnon-mediated phenomena.

AI.tldr: The authors develop a unified first-principles formalism for electron-magnon coupling (EMC) in collinear magnetic systems within many-body perturbation theory, complemented by machine-learning spinful Hamiltonians. Applied to ferromagnetic α-Fe, it recovers the full T² resistivity component with quantitative agreement to experiment, revealing that this term is dominated by EPC-EMC interplay rather than EMC alone. The framework also captures magnon-induced features in antiferromagnetic K-doped BaMn₂As₂, demonstrating general applicability.
AI.motivation: While electron-phonon coupling (EPC) is routinely treated in first-principles frameworks, no quantitative formalism exists for electron-magnon coupling (EMC), especially for transport. This gap leaves experimental discrepancies in magnetic materials—such as the missing T² resistivity in elemental iron—unexplained, with EMC long suspected but never computationally verified.
AI.method: The authors construct a unified first-principles formalism for EMC within many-body perturbation theory for collinear magnetic systems. They supplement this with machine-learning spinful Hamiltonians to obtain quantities not directly accessible from conventional first-principles calculations, enabling ab initio transport calculations that include EMC effects.
AI.result: For ferromagnetic α-Fe, the framework reproduces electron spectral functions consistent with prior studies and recovers the full T² resistivity component with a coefficient in quantitative agreement with measurements. Notably, the T² term is dominated by strong EPC-EMC interplay rather than EMC alone. For antiferromagnetic K-doped BaMn₂As₂, the method captures the ARPES-observed magnon-induced kink and a large EMC strength (~3) comparable to experiments.
AI.conclusion: The work closes a longstanding gap in quantitative understanding of transport in magnetic systems, provides the first ab initio transport calculations including EMC effects, and offers a predictive foundation for studying magnon-mediated phenomena such as unconventional superconductivity.

title: Local Well-Posedness of the Inviscid Shallow Water Equations with Surface Tension
summary: We show that the inviscid shallow water equations with gravity and surface tension are locally well-posed in dimensions one and two. In contrast to previous works by Benzoni-Gavage, Danchin, and Descombes, we work only in the real-valued phase space and make use of the symmetry of the system. Our alternative proof for local well-posedness sheds some light on the symmetric structure of the shallow water system and can be used for further study, including designing numerical scheme, dispersion estimate, etc.

AI.tldr: The paper proves local well-posedness for inviscid shallow water equations with gravity and surface tension in 1D and 2D, using a new approach that works in real-valued phase space and exploits the system's symmetry, unlike previous works that relied on different techniques.
AI.motivation: To provide an alternative proof of local well-posedness for inviscid shallow water equations with gravity and surface tension, which differs from previous approaches by Benzoni-Gavage, Danchin, and Descombes. The real-valued phase space approach and exploitation of symmetry offer new insights into the system's structure.
AI.method: The proof works entirely in the real-valued phase space and leverages the symmetric structure of the shallow water system, rather than relying on complex-valued techniques used in prior work.
AI.result: Local well-posedness is established for the inviscid shallow water equations with gravity and surface tension in dimensions one and two.
AI.conclusion: The alternative proof reveals the symmetric structure of the shallow water system, which can serve as a foundation for future work such as designing numerical schemes and deriving dispersion estimates.

title: Plasmon-polaritons in a rarefied nonrelativistic neutron gas
summary: The electromagnetic properties of a dilute unpolarized nonrelativistic neutron gas are described in the case when neutron-by-neutron scattering is negligible. The Gaussian (Maxwell-Boltzmann) and Fermi-Dirac one-particle density matrices for the neutron gas are considered, the typical space scale of variations of these density matrices being assumed to be much larger than the the typical space scale of variations of the electromagnetic field. The Green functions for the static effective Maxwell equations are obtained. The parameters of a nonequilibrium neutron gas are found where this gas possesses a ferromagnetic instability. The analog of Friedel oscillations is described. The properties of plasmon-polaritons in the neutron gas are revealed. It turns out that the dispersion law of longitudinal and transverse plasmon-polaritons has an infinite number of branches at a given momentum. The region of parameters where the plasmon-polaritons can be regarded as quasiparticles is found. The plasmon-polaritons on a Gaussian wave packet of a single electron are described. Their dispersion law proves to have an infinite number of branches at a given momentum. It is shown that there exist stable longitudinal plasmon-polaritons even on a single electron.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the electromagnetic properties of a dilute unpolarized nonrelativistic neutron gas where neutron-neutron scattering is negligible, examining density matrices, Green functions for effective Maxwell equations, ferromagnetic instability, Friedel oscillations, and plasmon-polaritons with infinite dispersion branches.
AI.motivation: To understand the electromagnetic response and collective excitations of a neutron gas, which, despite being electrically neutral, can exhibit interesting electromagnetic coupling through its magnetic moments and effective Maxwell equations.
AI.method: The authors use Gaussian (Maxwell-Boltzmann) and Fermi-Dirac one-particle density matrices for the neutron gas, assume that the spatial scale of density matrix variations is much larger than that of the electromagnetic field, and derive Green functions for static effective Maxwell equations. They also analyze plasmon-polaritons in the neutron gas and on Gaussian wave packets of single electrons.
AI.result: The dispersion law of longitudinal and transverse plasmon-polaritons has an infinite number of branches at a given momentum. Parameters for ferromagnetic instability in a nonequilibrium neutron gas are identified. Analog of Friedel oscillations is described, and stable longitudinal plasmon-polaritons are shown to exist even on a single electron.
AI.conclusion: The neutron gas exhibits complex electromagnetic properties including ferromagnetic instabilities under nonequilibrium conditions and plasmon-polariton excitations with infinitely many dispersion branches, some of which can be treated as quasiparticles in certain parameter regions.

title: Data-driven reduced-order models for the radiative transfer equation
summary: We present a data-driven reduced-order modeling (ROM) framework for the zeroth angular moment of the solution to the radiative transfer equation (RTE) rather than the full phase-space solution. Our construction is based on the Peierls integral formulation of the angularly averaged density. For media with isotropic scattering, the density satisfies a closed second-kind Fredholm equation with a globally attenuated, weakly singular kernel. We project this equation directly. For media with anisotropic scattering, we utilize the average-fluctuation decomposition to derive a closed system for a projection-based ROM. Numerical simulations are presented to illustrate the effectiveness of the ROMs we implemented.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a data-driven reduced-order modeling (ROM) framework for the zeroth angular moment (angularly averaged density) of the radiative transfer equation (RTE), using the Peierls integral formulation and projection-based methods for both isotropic and anisotropic scattering media.
AI.motivation: Full phase-space solutions to the radiative transfer equation are computationally expensive. A ROM targeting only the zeroth angular moment (angularly averaged density) offers significant computational savings while capturing the physically relevant quantity of interest.
AI.method: The method leverages the Peierls integral formulation of the angularly averaged density. For isotropic scattering, the density satisfies a closed second-kind Fredholm equation with a globally attenuated, weakly singular kernel, which is projected directly. For anisotropic scattering, an average-fluctuation decomposition derives a closed system for a projection-based ROM.
AI.result: Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the implemented reduced-order models.
AI.conclusion: The proposed data-driven ROM framework effectively reduces the computational cost of solving the RTE by projecting the Peierls integral formulation directly, rather than working with the full phase-space solution.

title: Power Series for the Quantum Statistical Mechanics Probability with Results for the Second Virial Coefficient of Helium
summary: A power series for the Wigner-Kirkwood pair commutation function for quantum statistical mechanics in classical phase space is given with terms automatically generated by recursion. The calculated second virial coefficient agrees with the measured values of helium for temperatures greater than 65 K. Prospects for a general quantum Monte Carlo algorithm are discussed.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a recursively generated power series for the Wigner-Kirkwood pair commutation function in quantum statistical mechanics, demonstrating agreement with measured helium virial coefficients above 65 K and discussing potential quantum Monte Carlo applications.
AI.motivation: The need to compute quantum corrections to classical statistical mechanics expressions, particularly for the second virial coefficient, in a systematic and automated way.
AI.method: A power series expansion for the Wigner-Kirkwood pair commutation function is developed, with terms generated automatically via a recursion scheme.
AI.result: The calculated second virial coefficient matches experimental values for helium at temperatures greater than 65 K.
AI.conclusion: The recursion-based power series approach is validated for helium virial coefficients, and the authors discuss the potential for developing a general quantum Monte Carlo algorithm based on this framework.

title: Orbital instability of solitary waves for the generalized BBM equation at the negative critical endpoint
summary: We study the orbital stability of solitary waves to the generalized Benjamin--Bona--Mahony equation $$ u_t+u_x+κ\frac{p+1}{2}(u^p)_x-u_{txx}=0, \qquad (t,x)\in\mathbb R^+\times\mathbb R, $$ where $κ\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$ and $p\geq2$ is an integer. This equation admits solitary waves of the form $$ u(t,x)=φ_c(x-ct). $$ At the negative critical endpoint speed $$ c=c_p^-= \frac{p-1}{2(p+1)} \left(1-\sqrt{\frac{p+3}{2}}\right)<0, $$ we prove that the corresponding solitary wave is orbitally unstable whenever either $κ<0$, or $κ>0$ and $p$ is even. The proof combines a codimension-two coercivity estimate, two-parameter modulation, and a corrected localized virial functional adapted to the degeneracy of the momentum slope at the endpoint.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the orbital stability of solitary waves for the generalized Benjamin-Bona-Mahony (gBBM) equation and proves that at a specific negative critical endpoint speed, the solitary waves are orbitally unstable under certain parameter conditions.
AI.motivation: To determine the orbital stability/instability of solitary waves in the gBBM equation at a degenerate critical endpoint speed where the momentum slope vanishes, which requires novel analytical techniques beyond standard stability theory.
AI.method: The proof combines three key ingredients: a codimension-two coercivity estimate, two-parameter modulation, and a corrected localized virial functional adapted to the degeneracy of the momentum slope at the endpoint.
AI.result: It is proven that the solitary wave is orbitally unstable at the critical endpoint speed c_p^- whenever either κ<0, or κ>0 and p is even.
AI.conclusion: The instability result covers the negative critical endpoint speed for specific parameter regimes, resolving the stability question in these cases through a refined analytical framework.

title: Wavefront-Guided Electron Injection for Direct Laser Acceleration in Relativistic Laser-Driven Plasma Channel
summary: We investigate electron injection into direct laser acceleration (DLA) in relativistic laser-driven plasma channels using particle-in-cell simulations. We identify and characterize a wavefront-guided injection mechanism, in which electrons are continuously fed into the plasma channel through the density pile-up layer at the laser-pulse front. Phase-space analysis reveals a localized injectable region within the pile-up layer, indicating that only a selected subset of electrons satisfies the conditions required for the subsequent direct laser acceleration. This mechanism provides a physical interpretation for the high-charge capability of DLA by explaining how electrons are continuously supplied to the accelerating channel. Beyond this continuous supply process, the injection dynamics are further modulated by the periodic variation of the carrier phase at the laser-pulse front. The spatial locations of injected electrons are found to be closely associated with magnetic-island structures formed under laser-phase modulation, suggesting that the laser wavefront not only supplies electrons but also organizes their entry into the accelerating channel. These findings advance the physical understanding of energetic-electron generation in relativistic laser-driven subcritical-density plasma channels and are relevant to the development of compact DLA-based particle and radiation sources.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates electron injection into direct laser acceleration (DLA) in relativistic laser-driven plasma channels via particle-in-cell simulations, identifying a wavefront-guided injection mechanism where electrons are continuously fed into the channel through the density pile-up layer at the laser pulse front. The authors find that carrier-phase modulation and magnetic-island structures organize electron entry, providing a physical interpretation for DLA's high-charge capability.
AI.motivation: To understand how electrons are continuously supplied to the accelerating channel in direct laser acceleration, which is key to explaining the high-charge capability of DLA and advancing compact particle/radiation source development.
AI.method: Particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of relativistic laser-driven plasma channels, combined with phase-space analysis to identify injectable regions within the density pile-up layer and examination of laser-phase-modulated injection dynamics.
AI.result: Identification of a wavefront-guided injection mechanism where a localized injectable region exists in the pile-up layer, selecting a subset of electrons for DLA. Carrier-phase modulation organizes electron entry, and injected electron locations correlate with magnetic-island structures formed under laser-phase modulation.
AI.conclusion: The laser wavefront both supplies and organizes electron injection into the DLA channel, advancing physical understanding of energetic-electron generation in relativistic laser-driven subcritical-density plasmas and informing compact DLA-based source development.

title: On Convergence of an Accelerated Modified Newton Method for Nonlinear Equations
summary: Newton's iteration is a fundamental tool for root-finding and numerical solutions of systems of equations. The iteration rapidly refines the initial approximation to the exact root, and in general the convergence is quadratic. Since the method requires finding the function value and its derivative at each iteration, in some cases, it may not converge. This is because the value of the derivative gets close to zero. In this paper, we introduce a modified and stable algorithm of Newton's iteration method that addresses this issue, reduces computational cost, and improves efficiency. In addition. we analyze the convergence properties of the modified method to demonstrate its effectiveness.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a modified, stable version of Newton's iteration method for root-finding that addresses the failure of convergence when derivatives approach zero, reduces computational cost, and improves overall efficiency.
AI.motivation: Standard Newton's iteration can fail to converge when the derivative value gets close to zero during iteration, which limits its practical applicability in solving systems of equations.
AI.method: A modified and stable algorithm of Newton's iteration method is proposed, designed to handle near-zero derivative situations while lowering computational cost.
AI.result: The modified method demonstrates convergence properties that confirm its effectiveness, addressing the derivative-zero issue and improving efficiency over the classical approach.
AI.conclusion: The proposed modified Newton's method is a viable, more stable, and computationally efficient alternative to the classical Newton's iteration for root-finding applications.

title: Liouville theorems and symmetry of positive solutions for partially confined nonlinear Schrödinger equations
summary:
This paper studies positive solutions to the stationary nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a partial harmonic confinement: $$-Δu + \big( x_1^2 + \cdots + x_d^2 \big) u + λu = g(u), \qquad u \in H^1(\mathbb{R}^N),$$ where $1 \leq d \leq N-1$, and the nonlinearity $g(u)\geq 0$ satisfies standard regularity and subcritical growth conditions. While previous works only studied the case $λ\geq 0$, here by applying a spectral analysis of the Schrödinger operator $H=-Δ+|y|^2, y=(x_1,\cdots,x_d)$, together with the variational method and moving planes method, we prove that \begin{itemize} \item A necessary condition for the existence of positive solutions is $λ\geq -d$, and there are no positive solutions for the zero-mass case $λ=-d$ as long as $N-d\leq 4$. \item For $λ>-d$, this equation admits at least one positive solution. Moreover, any positive solution must be radially symmetric and decreasing with respect to the first $d$ (confined) variables $y=(x_1,\cdots,x_d)$, and is also radially symmetric and decreasing, up to a translation, with respect to the remaining $N-d$ (unconfined) variables. \end{itemize}
  \vskip 0.2in Dedicated to our supervisor Prof. Wenming Zou on the occasion of his 60th birthday.

AI.tldr: This paper studies positive solutions of a stationary nonlinear Schrödinger equation with partial harmonic confinement, proving existence for λ > -d and nonexistence for the zero-mass case λ = -d when N-d ≤ 4. It also establishes symmetry properties of positive solutions using variational methods and the moving planes method.
AI.motivation: Previous works on this equation with partial harmonic confinement only considered the case λ ≥ 0. The authors aim to extend the analysis to negative values of λ, which requires a spectral analysis of the Schrödinger operator H = -Δ + |y|² and a deeper understanding of the existence, nonexistence, and symmetry properties of positive solutions.
AI.method: The authors combine spectral analysis of the operator H = -Δ + |y|² with variational methods to establish existence results, and employ the moving planes method to derive symmetry properties of positive solutions.
AI.result: (1) A necessary condition for existence is λ ≥ -d, and no positive solutions exist for λ = -d when N-d ≤ 4. (2) For λ > -d, at least one positive solution exists. Furthermore, any positive solution is radially symmetric and decreasing in the confined variables y = (x₁,...,x_d), and radially symmetric and decreasing up to translation in the unconfined variables.
AI.conclusion: The paper fully characterizes the threshold of λ for existence of positive solutions (λ > -d) and establishes both existence and symmetry results, significantly extending previous work that only covered λ ≥ 0.

title: Interpretable statistical feature engineering for early disruption prediction in the short pulse ADITYA tokamak
summary: Reliable early disruption prediction is critical for the safe operation and real-time control of tokamaks. However, machine learning based prediction frameworks have predominantly targeted medium and long pulse devices, with comparatively limited attention given to short pulse tokamaks where available warning time is inherently constrained. In this work, an interpretable machine learning framework is developed for feature engineering and early prediction of disruptions in the ADITYA using the initial plasma evolution information, prior to the activation of the negative converter of the ohmic transformer power supply. Statistical descriptors comprising the mean, variance, skewness, kurtosis and wavelet energy entropy are extracted from routinely available plasma diagnostics over different operation time windows. Decision tree based feature selection is employed to identify physically meaningful disruption precursors and to reduce feature dimensionality. These selected features are used to train a random forest classifier. The proposed framework achieves stable predictive performance across different analysis windows, with a maximum ROC-AUC of 0.87 for 0-35 ms and 0-40 ms windows. Comparable and in some cases improved, performance is obtained using the reduced feature set, demonstrating that the selected statistical descriptors retain the essential information required for disruption prediction. The proposed methodology provides an interpretable and computationally efficient framework for real time disruption prediction in short pulse tokamaks and establishes that carefully engineered statistical descriptors can effectively replace raw time series inputs for early disruption prediction, thereby offering a practical pathway toward real time plasma control in short pulse tokamaks similar to ADITYA and ADITYA-U.

AI.tldr: An interpretable machine learning framework is developed for early disruption prediction in the short-pulse ADITYA tokamak, using statistical descriptors (mean, variance, skewness, kurtosis, wavelet energy entropy) from plasma diagnostics prior to negative converter activation. Decision tree feature selection reduces dimensionality, and a random forest classifier achieves ROC-AUC up to 0.87, demonstrating that engineered statistical features can effectively replace raw time-series inputs for real-time disruption prediction.
AI.motivation: Machine learning disruption prediction frameworks have focused on medium/long pulse tokamaks, leaving short-pulse devices under-addressed where warning time is limited and real-time prediction is especially challenging.
AI.method: Statistical descriptors are extracted from plasma diagnostics over different operation time windows; decision tree-based feature selection identifies physically meaningful precursors; selected features train a random forest classifier.
AI.result: Maximum ROC-AUC of 0.87 for 0-35 ms and 0-40 ms windows with stable performance; reduced feature sets achieve comparable or improved results.
AI.conclusion: Carefully engineered statistical descriptors can replace raw time series inputs for early disruption prediction, providing an interpretable and computationally efficient pathway for real-time plasma control in short-pulse tokamaks like ADITYA and ADITYA-U.

title: A posteriori error estimates for the two-step explicit exponential Adams method for parabolic equations
summary: In this paper, we derive optimal order a posteriori error estimates for the variable step-size explicit two-step exponential Adams (E-Adams2) method for parabolic problems. We begin by introducing an E-Adams2 approximation, deffned by the piecewise linear approximate solutions, which leads to suboptimal error estimates. To recover optimal order error estimates, we introducean appropriate reconstruction of the approximation with the second order residual for the explicit E-Adams2 method, which plays key roles in deriving optimal order a posteriori error estimates for the proposed explicit method for linear and semilinear parabolic equations. Various numerical experiments are carried out to verify the correct convergence rates of the a posteriori quantities, and the high efffciency of the adaptive algorithm.

AI.tldr: The paper derives optimal-order a posteriori error estimates for the variable step-size explicit two-step exponential Adams (E-Adams2) method applied to parabolic problems, using a reconstruction technique with second-order residual to achieve optimal error bounds, verified through numerical experiments.
AI.motivation: To obtain optimal-order a posteriori error estimates for the explicit E-Adams2 method for parabolic problems, since the standard piecewise linear approximation approach only yields suboptimal error estimates.
AI.method: The authors first define an E-Adams2 approximation using piecewise linear approximate solutions (which gives suboptimal estimates), then introduce an appropriate reconstruction of the approximation with second-order residual to recover optimal-order a posteriori error estimates for both linear and semilinear parabolic equations.
AI.result: Numerical experiments verify the correct convergence rates of the a posteriori estimators and demonstrate the high efficiency of the adaptive algorithm.
AI.conclusion: The proposed reconstruction-based approach successfully yields optimal-order a posteriori error estimates for the explicit E-Adams2 method, providing a reliable foundation for adaptive time-stepping in parabolic problems.
