  First, per-call cost and share of runtime are different quantities, and only the second bounds acceleration. An exclusive self-time profile puts the target block at 16.9% of critical-rank wall clock, capping any surrogate at ~1.2x by Amdahl's law. A surrogate 5.8x cheaper per call merely ties the solver, and the configuration stable enough to run without fallback reaches only parity. Second, offline accuracy cannot rank surrogates for deployment: across fourteen networks the pooled Spearman error-versus-survival correlation (rho = +0.73) is a between-family confound that vanishes under control (rho = -0.04). Third, a correct out-of-distribution gate cannot accelerate a loop that leaves its training distribution. We give the break-even deferral fraction in closed form: because the visited states sit 73x off the data manifold, the gate defers 96.8 to 99.7% of cells, almost invariant to surrogate quality. Including its own cost, the gated loop is a 0.94 to 0.96x slowdown.
  We further separate stability from fidelity: a never-crashing gated run accumulates a linear -19.9% density bias over 6000 steps. The error is a directed, ballistically accumulating bias, not the variance-driven divergence the autoregressive literature targets.

AI.tldr: The paper reports a controlled, end-to-end negative result for learned surrogates replacing an expensive implicit Newton solver in general-relativistic radiation-hydrodynamics, identifying three structural barriers: (1) runtime share (16.9%) rather than per-call cost caps speedup at ~1.2x by Amdahl's law; (2) offline accuracy cannot rank deployment-worthy surrogates (Spearman correlation vanishes under control); (3) an out-of-distribution gate cannot accelerate a loop that leaves its training distribution, deferring 96.8-99.7% of cells and causing a 0.94-0.96x slowdown. Stable gated runs also accumulate a linear -19.9% density bias (a directed bias, not variance-driven divergence).
AI.motivation: To investigate whether learned surrogates for expensive inner solver blocks can actually accelerate multiphysics simulation, using a rigorous end-to-end controlled study on the most expensive physics routine (implicit Newton solve coupling neutrino radiation to matter) in a GR radiation-hydrodynamics code.
AI.method: Controlled end-to-end evaluation: exclusive self-time profiling, Amdahl's law analysis, training fourteen surrogate networks, offline vs. online accuracy comparisons with pooled and controlled Spearman correlations, an out-of-distribution gate with break-even deferral fraction analysis, and long-run stability tracking for density bias.
AI.result: Three structural barriers identified: per-call cost is not runtime share (16.9% caps acceleration at ~1.2x; a 5.8x cheaper per-call surrogate only ties); offline accuracy does not rank deployment surrogates (pooled rho=+0.73 vanishes to rho=-0.04 under control); the OOD gate defers 96.8-99.7% of cells due to 73x off-manifold states, yielding a 0.94-0.96x slowdown. A stable gated run accumulates a linear -19.9% density bias, a directed ballistic bias rather than variance-driven divergence.
AI.conclusion: The negative result is not due to network deficiency but to structural barriers inherent to surrogate-for-solver substitution in this setting: runtime-share caps, non-transferable offline metrics, and distribution shift that defeats gating. The work also separates stability from fidelity, showing that a never-crashing surrogate can still produce significant systematic bias.

title: A small rigid body immersed in a three-dimensional viscous fluid and the vanishing viscosity limit
summary: In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of a coupled fluid--rigid body system, consisting of a rigid body immersed in a three-dimensional viscous incompressible fluid, as the body size and the fluid viscosity vanish. We prove that the limiting velocity field is governed by the whole-space incompressible Euler equations. Moreover, the influence of the fluid on the rigid body motion is shown to vanish in this limit.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the asymptotic limit of a coupled fluid-rigid body system in 3D as both the body size and fluid viscosity tend to zero, proving that the limiting velocity field satisfies the whole-space incompressible Euler equations and that fluid influence on the rigid body motion vanishes.
AI.motivation: To understand the limiting behavior of a fluid-rigid body interaction system when both the rigid body shrinks and viscosity diminishes, determining whether the system converges to a simpler Euler flow description.
AI.method: Mathematical analysis of the coupled fluid-rigid body system in three dimensions, deriving the asymptotic limit as body size and viscosity simultaneously vanish, and proving convergence to the incompressible Euler equations.
AI.result: The limiting velocity field is governed by the whole-space incompressible Euler equations, and the fluid's influence on the rigid body motion vanishes in this limit.
AI.conclusion: In the combined limit of vanishing body size and viscosity, the coupled system reduces to the incompressible Euler equations, with the rigid body's effect on the fluid becoming negligible.

title: A variational framework for bond-based peridynamics with spatially varying horizons and its asynchronous time integration
summary:
Bond-based peridynamics provides a non-local framework for modelling fracture without requiring spatial derivatives of the displacement field. However, when spatially varying horizons are used together with non-uniform discretisations, the classical single-horizon bond-based peridynamics formulation leads to asymmetric interactions between material points. These asymmetric interactions violate balance laws and can introduce non-physical artefacts such as ghost forces and spurious wave reflections. In this work, we develop a variational formulation for bond-based peridynamics with spatially varying horizons. Starting from the Lagrange-d'Alembert principle, we derive the governing equations of motion and show that the dual-horizon peridynamics formulation emerges naturally from the variation of the internal energy.
  Building on this variational structure, we construct asynchronous variational integrators that allow different time step sizes in different regions of the domain. This is particularly useful for dynamic fracture simulations with local refinement, where small time steps are required only near regions of high resolution or expected crack growth. Numerical examples involving wave propagation, a pre-cracked plate under tension, and the Kalthoff-Winkler impact experiment demonstrate that the proposed framework removes spurious reflections caused by non-uniform horizons, preserves physically consistent fracture patterns, and achieves results comparable to uniformly refined simulations. At the same time, the asynchronous variational integrator reduces the number of internal force evaluations compared to the standard velocity-Verlet method. The proposed approach therefore provides a consistent variational foundation and an efficient time-integration strategy for bond-based peridynamic simulations with spatially varying horizons.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a variational formulation for bond-based peridynamics with spatially varying horizons, showing that dual-horizon peridynamics emerges naturally from the variation of internal energy. The authors construct asynchronous variational integrators enabling different time steps in different regions, removing spurious reflections, preserving fracture patterns, and reducing computational cost versus velocity-Verlet.
AI.motivation: Classical single-horizon bond-based peridynamics with spatially varying horizons and non-uniform discretizations leads to asymmetric interactions that violate balance laws and introduce non-physical artefacts such as ghost forces and spurious wave reflections.
AI.method: Starting from the Lagrange-d'Alembert principle, the authors derive governing equations of motion and show dual-horizon peridynamics emerges from the variation of internal energy. They then construct asynchronous variational integrators that allow different time step sizes in different regions of the domain.
AI.result: Numerical examples (wave propagation, pre-cracked plate under tension, Kalthoff-Winkler impact experiment) demonstrate removal of spurious reflections, physically consistent fracture patterns comparable to uniformly refined simulations, and reduced number of internal force evaluations compared to velocity-Verlet.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach provides a consistent variational foundation and an efficient time-integration strategy for bond-based peridynamic simulations with spatially varying horizons.

title: A simple derivation of Anderson-Hartree equations with harmonic potential
summary: In this paper, we show how to adapt a derivation of Hartree equations due to Knowles and Pickl in the case where the one-particle hamiltonian is an Anderson-Hermite operator in dimension 1 and 2 or a formal Anderson-Hermite operator in dimension 3. By proving energy estimates for solution of the limit equation, uniform in the noise in bounded sets, we achieve a double limit. Namely, we show that we can commute the mean-field limit with a limit in noise.

AI.tldr: The paper shows how to adapt a derivation of Hartree equations (from Knowles and Pickl) to cases where the one-particle Hamiltonian is an Anderson-Hermite operator in 1D and 2D, or a formal Anderson-Hermite operator in 3D. By proving noise-uniform energy estimates, the authors achieve a double limit, demonstrating that the mean-field limit and the noise limit can be interchanged.
AI.motivation: To understand whether the mean-field limit (relevant for many-body quantum systems) can be taken simultaneously or interchangeably with a noise limit (relevant for disordered systems described by Anderson-type operators). This addresses a fundamental question about the interplay between quantum many-body dynamics and disorder.
AI.method: The authors adapt the Knowles-Pickl derivation of Hartree equations to Anderson-Hermite operators. They prove energy estimates for solutions of the limit (Hartree) equation that are uniform in the noise over bounded sets. This uniformity of estimates enables them to establish a double limit, allowing the mean-field limit and the noise limit to be commuted.
AI.result: The paper demonstrates that the mean-field limit and the noise limit can be interchanged (commuted) for Anderson-Hermite operators in dimensions 1 and 2, and for formal Anderson-Hermite operators in dimension 3.
AI.conclusion: The mean-field and disorder (noise) limits commute in this setting, which is significant because it shows that the order in which one takes these two limits does not affect the resulting effective dynamics described by Hartree equations.

title: Symmetric Taylor--Hood elements for the linear stress gradient problem
summary: We develop mixed finite element methods for the linear stress-gradient elasticity problem based on symmetric Taylor--Hood elements. We establish the stability of the symmetric Taylor--Hood pair on simplicial meshes in both two and three dimensions, thereby resolving the stability left open by Brezzi, Fortin, and Marini in 1993. Combing the Nitsche's method, we further construct finite element schemes for linear stress problem in general boundary condition. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.

AI.tldr: This paper develops mixed finite element methods for linear stress-gradient elasticity using symmetric Taylor-Hood elements, proves stability on simplicial meshes in 2D and 3D (resolving an open problem from Brezzi, Fortin, and Marini 1993), and extends the approach to general boundary conditions via Nitsche's method, with numerical experiments confirming the theory.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to resolve a long-standing open problem in the stability of symmetric Taylor-Hood elements for stress-gradient elasticity problems, which was left open by Brezzi, Fortin, and Marini in 1993.
AI.method: The method uses symmetric Taylor-Hood elements for mixed finite element discretization of linear stress-gradient elasticity. Stability is established on simplicial meshes in both 2D and 3D. Nitsche's method is combined to handle general boundary conditions in the resulting finite element schemes.
AI.result: The paper proves the stability of the symmetric Taylor-Hood pair on simplicial meshes in both two and three dimensions, resolving the open stability question. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.
AI.conclusion: The stability of symmetric Taylor-Hood elements for stress-gradient elasticity is established, and the method is extended to general boundary conditions using Nitsche's method, with numerical validation of all theoretical findings.

title: No bubble trees for the $1$-equivariant harmonic map heat flow and the radial energy-critical nonlinear heat equation in low dimensions
summary: We consider the $1$-equivariant harmonic map heat flow (HMHF) from $\mathbb R^2$ to $\mathbb S^2$ and the radial energy-critical nonlinear heat equation (NLH) in dimensions $d=3,4,5$. We prove that every finite-energy solution of (HMHF) and every $\dot H^1$-bounded solution of (NLH) has at most one bubble: every finite-time blow-up has exactly one bubble, whereas every global solution has either no bubble or one bubble at infinite time. Starting from the soliton resolution, we exclude bubble trees by modulation analysis, deriving a contradiction from the relative dynamics of the two innermost scales. This energy method does not rely on maximum principle and, in particular, applies without restriction on the bubble signs.

AI.tldr: The paper proves that finite-energy solutions of the 1-equivariant harmonic map heat flow and H^1-bounded solutions of the radial energy-critical nonlinear heat equation have at most one bubble: finite-time blow-ups have exactly one bubble, while global solutions have either none or one at infinite time. The proof excludes bubble trees via modulation analysis on the two innermost scales, using an energy method that does not rely on maximum principle and applies without sign restrictions.
AI.motivation: To resolve the question of whether multiple bubbles (bubble trees) can form in these critical parabolic equations, which is a fundamental question about the structure of singularities and the soliton resolution conjecture.
AI.method: Starting from soliton resolution, the authors exclude bubble trees by modulation analysis. They derive a contradiction from the relative dynamics of the two innermost scales, using an energy method that avoids the maximum principle, making it applicable to arbitrary bubble signs.
AI.result: Every finite-energy solution of HMHF has at most one bubble; every finite-time blow-up has exactly one bubble, and every global solution has either no bubble or one bubble at infinite time. The same holds for H^1-bounded NLH solutions in dimensions 3, 4, 5.
AI.conclusion: Bubble trees cannot occur in these settings, establishing a sharp at-most-one-bubble result for both the harmonic map heat flow and the energy-critical nonlinear heat equation, with a proof valid for arbitrary bubble signs.

title: First-Principles Spin-Lattice Coupling from Downfolded Electron-Phonon Interaction
summary: We present a method to calculate spin-phonon coupling parameters from first-principles perturbation theory by downfolding the electron-phonon coupling (EPC). We exploit the localized nature of magnetic moments and atomic displacements by working in the Wannier representation of the electronic Hamiltonian and the EPC matrix. The spin system is mapped to a classical Heisenberg Hamiltonian, whose parameters are obtained by treating local spin rotations as a perturbation within a Green's-function formalism. The spin and phonon perturbations are connected through the EPC parameters, which enter as lattice-induced perturbations to the tight-binding Hamiltonian. By combining these lattice perturbations with local spin rotations, we obtain real-space derivatives of magnetic exchange parameters without performing displaced magnetic supercell calculations. We illustrate the method on SrMnO$_3$ and show that it can be integrated directly into standard workflows.

AI.tldr: A first-principles method to compute spin-phonon coupling parameters by downfolding electron-phonon coupling into a Wannier representation, mapping the spin system to a classical Heisenberg Hamiltonian, and deriving real-space derivatives of magnetic exchange parameters without displaced magnetic supercell calculations. Demonstrated on SrMnO3.
AI.motivation: To enable efficient and accurate calculation of spin-phonon coupling parameters from first principles, avoiding the need for computationally expensive displaced magnetic supercell calculations.
AI.method: The method downfolds the electron-phonon coupling (EPC) using the Wannier representation of the electronic Hamiltonian, treats local spin rotations as perturbations within a Green's-function formalism to map the spin system to a classical Heisenberg Hamiltonian, and combines lattice perturbations with local spin rotations to obtain real-space derivatives of magnetic exchange parameters.
AI.result: The method is illustrated on SrMnO3 and shown to integrate directly into standard workflows, demonstrating its practical applicability.
AI.conclusion: The approach provides a first-principles framework for computing spin-phonon coupling parameters efficiently by exploiting the localized nature of magnetic moments and atomic displacements, without requiring displaced magnetic supercell calculations.

title: The Global Weak-Lorentz Vorticity Endpoint in the Stationary Navier--Stokes Liouville Problem
summary:
Let $(v,p)$ be a smooth stationary Navier--Stokes flow in $\mathbb R^3$ that vanishes at infinity, and set $ω:=\operatorname{curl}v$. We prove the endpoint implication \[
  ω\in L^{9/5,\infty}(\mathbb R^3)
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad v\equiv0. \] This weak-Lorentz condition is invariant under the far-field rescaling associated with the borderline vorticity decay $|ω(x)|=O(|x|^{-5/3})$ and strictly extends the $L^{9/5}$ vorticity criterion of Chae--Wolf. It also removes the relative smallness condition from the critical pointwise criterion of Kozono--Terasawa--Wakasugi: the decay $|ω(x)|=O(|x|^{-5/3})$ alone implies $v\equiv0$. No finite Dirichlet energy is assumed. In our proof, we firstly use the endpoint Biot--Savart mapping and the critical annular Lorentz estimate of Seregin--Wang to yield finite Dirichlet energy. A logarithmic bound for the cumulative $L^{9/5}$ mass then selects blow-down scales whose stationary Euler limit satisfies Bernoulli companion laws on the exterior region. Together with the inherited weak endpoint bounds, these laws force the limiting energy flux to vanish. A harmonic-cutoff identity transfers this vanishing to the original scale and yields zero Dirichlet energy.

AI.tldr: The paper proves that if a smooth stationary Navier-Stokes flow in R³ vanishing at infinity has vorticity in the weak Lorentz space L^{9/5,∞}, then the flow must be identically zero. This extends prior criteria of Chae-Wolf and Kozono-Terasawa-Wakasugi by removing smallness conditions and using a scale-invariant weak-Lorentz assumption without requiring finite Dirichlet energy.
AI.motivation: To establish a sharp, scale-invariant endpoint criterion for triviality of stationary Navier-Stokes flows based solely on weak Lorentz vorticity decay, extending earlier results that required stronger L^{9/5} integrability or additional smallness/pointwise decay assumptions.
AI.method: The proof proceeds in several steps: (1) use the endpoint Biot-Savart mapping and Seregin-Wang's critical annular Lorentz estimate to establish finite Dirichlet energy; (2) obtain a logarithmic bound for cumulative L^{9/5} vorticity mass to select blow-down scales; (3) show the stationary Euler limit satisfies Bernoulli companion laws on the exterior region; (4) combine these with inherited weak endpoint bounds to force zero energy flux in the limit; (5) use a harmonic-cutoff identity to transfer the vanishing energy flux back to the original scale, yielding zero Dirichlet energy and hence v ≡ 0.
AI.result: The endpoint implication ω ∈ L^{9/5,∞}(R³) ⇒ v ≡ 0 is proven for smooth stationary Navier-Stokes flows vanishing at infinity, without assuming finite Dirichlet energy. This strictly extends the Chae-Wolf L^{9/5} criterion and removes the relative smallness condition from the Kozono-Terasawa-Wakasugi critical pointwise criterion.
AI.conclusion: A pure weak-Lorentz vorticity decay condition, invariant under the far-field rescaling associated with borderline vorticity decay |ω(x)| = O(|x|^{-5/3}), is sufficient by itself to force triviality of the stationary Navier-Stokes flow. The result is optimal in scale and removes all previous smallness or energy assumptions.

title: A Fully Matrix-Free Three-Grid Preconditioner for the Time-Harmonic Maxwell Equations at Extreme Scale
summary: Three-dimensional time-harmonic Maxwell simulations generate massive complex indefinite systems whose mesh coarsening is strictly limited by phase accuracy. Although matrix-free finite element kernels utilize GPU throughput efficiently, standard multilevel solvers are ultimately bottlenecked by the memory and communication costs of exact coarse-grid factorizations. We present a fully matrix-free, factorization-free three-grid preconditioner for curl-conforming N{é}delec discretizations with perfectly matched layers (PML) and optimally blended quadrature. The method employs an outer FGMRES to solve the unshifted fine-grid equation, while an intermediate-grid correction is computed by a fixed-work FGMRES preconditioned with a complex-shifted $2h$--$4h$ cycle. This strategically confines the complex shift to an auxiliary preconditioner, preserving the physical Maxwell operator. A local Fourier analysis derives the blended Maxwell branches and compatible edge transfers, identifying robust shift and Jacobi damping parameters. Validated against the analytical Maxwell Green tensor, our approach demonstrates extreme scalability: using a single solver configuration, both homogeneous and highly heterogeneous systems with approximately 10.89 billion complex edge unknowns are solved in 42.0--72.0 seconds on just 64 NVIDIA A100 GPUs.

AI.tldr: A fully matrix-free, factorization-free three-grid preconditioner for large-scale time-harmonic Maxwell simulations, achieving extreme scalability (10.89 billion unknowns solved in 42-72 seconds on 64 GPUs).
AI.motivation: Standard multilevel solvers for time-harmonic Maxwell systems are bottlenecked by memory and communication costs of exact coarse-grid factorizations, while mesh coarsening is limited by phase accuracy requirements.
AI.method: A three-grid preconditioner with: (1) outer FGMRES on the fine grid, (2) intermediate-grid correction via fixed-work FGMRES preconditioned with a complex-shifted 2h-4h cycle, (3) complex shift confined to an auxiliary preconditioner, with parameters derived through local Fourier analysis.
AI.result: Using a single solver configuration, both homogeneous and highly heterogeneous systems with ~10.89 billion complex edge unknowns are solved in 42.0-72.0 seconds on 64 NVIDIA A100 GPUs, validated against the analytical Maxwell Green tensor.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach demonstrates extreme scalability for large-scale Maxwell simulations without requiring coarse-grid factorizations, preserving the physical Maxwell operator while achieving fast solution times.

title: Quantum Hydrodynamic Framework of Coherent Terahertz Emission in MXenes Driven via Engineered Femtosecond Waveforms
summary: Coherent terahertz (THz) emitters based on low dimensional quantum materials have attracted significant interest for compact broadband photonic technologies. However, theoretical descriptions that consistently connect microscopic quantum dynamics to emitted THz radiation remain limited for MXenes, whose electronic properties are governed by transition metal d orbitals and chemically tunable surface terminations. A multiscale density-matrix formalism for coherent THz generation in metallic MXenes driven by engineered three color femtosecond waveforms is developed. Material-specific electronic structures are described by parameterized multiband tight binding Hamiltonians, while ultrafast carrier dynamics are treated using a non-secular Redfield master equation that explicitly retains interband coherence, carrier populations, electron phonon interactions, impurity scattering, and environment-induced relaxation. The transient photocurrent is explicitly decomposed into population and coherence driven contributions and linked to the emitted THz field through its time derivative, establishing a direct connection between microscopic quantum dynamics and macroscopic radiation. The results show that environmental coupling does not merely attenuate THz emission, but redistributes coherent and population currents and reshapes the emitted waveform in both the time and frequency domains. Systematic investigations of optical waveform parameters, effective electronic structure, and open system relaxation identify physically grounded strategies for enhancing broadband THz generation. The proposed methodology establishes a transferable microscopic design platform for connecting material specific electronic structure, quantum coherence, open system relaxation, nonlinear carrier transport, and coherent THz emission across MXenes and related low dimensional quantum materials.

AI.tldr: A multiscale density-matrix formalism is developed to connect microscopic quantum dynamics (material-specific tight-binding Hamiltonians for MXenes, non-secular Redfield master equation for carrier dynamics) to macroscopic coherent THz emission driven by three-color femtosecond waveforms. The work shows environmental coupling redistributes coherent vs. population currents rather than simply attenuating emission, and identifies strategies for enhancing broadband THz generation.
AI.motivation: Coherent THz emitters from low-dimensional quantum materials are promising for compact broadband photonics, but theoretical frameworks linking microscopic quantum dynamics to emitted THz radiation are lacking for MXenes—whose properties depend on transition metal d orbitals and tunable surface terminations.
AI.method: Develops a multiscale density-matrix formalism combining: (1) parameterized multiband tight-binding Hamiltonians for material-specific electronic structure, and (2) a non-secular Redfield master equation capturing ultrafast carrier dynamics including interband coherence, populations, electron-phonon interactions, impurity scattering, and environment-induced relaxation. The transient photocurrent is decomposed into population- and coherence-driven contributions and linked to THz emission via its time derivative.
AI.result: Environmental coupling does not merely attenuate THz emission but redistributes coherent and population currents and reshapes the emitted waveform in both time and frequency domains. Systematic studies of optical waveform parameters, electronic structure, and open system relaxation reveal physically grounded strategies for enhancing broadband THz generation.
AI.conclusion: The methodology establishes a transferable microscopic design platform connecting material-specific electronic structure, quantum coherence, open system relaxation, nonlinear carrier transport, and coherent THz emission for MXenes and related low-dimensional quantum materials.

title: Uniqueness for the Degenerate Monge-Ampère Equation on Arbitrary Bounded Convex Domains
summary:
Let $n\ge2$ and let $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$ be an arbitrary bounded open convex set. The author prove that, for $p>n$, the Dirichlet problem \[
  \det D^2u=(-u)^p\quad\text{in }Ω,
  \qquad u=0\quad\text{on }\partialΩ,
  \qquad u>0\quad\text{in }Ω\] has at most one convex Alexandrov solution. The proof is based on the affine behavior of the Monge--Ampère energy and on a power-concavity property of the $L^{p+1}$ mass along the Legendre path connecting two solutions. At the homogeneous exponent $p=n$, the same argument shows that any two nonzero solutions with the same coefficient are positive multiples of one another.

AI.tldr: The paper proves uniqueness of convex Alexandrov solutions to the Dirichlet problem for the Monge-Ampère equation det D²u = (-u)^p with p > n on any bounded open convex domain, using affine invariance of the Monge-Ampère energy and power-concavity of L^{p+1} mass along Legendre paths. At p = n, solutions with the same coefficient are shown to be scalar multiples.
AI.motivation: To establish uniqueness of solutions to a singular/degenerate Monge-Ampère Dirichlet problem with a power-type right-hand side, which is a fundamental question for this class of nonlinear elliptic equations in general convex domains.
AI.method: The proof leverages the affine (linear) behavior of the Monge-Ampère energy and a power-concavity property of the L^{p+1} mass along the Legendre (Legendre-Fenchel transform) path connecting two solutions. This geometric/energetic framework is used to rule out multiplicity for p > n, and to show scaling relations at the critical exponent p = n.
AI.result: For p > n, there is at most one convex Alexandrov solution to the problem. For p = n, any two nonzero solutions sharing the same coefficient are positive multiples of one another.
AI.conclusion: The uniqueness result holds on arbitrary bounded open convex sets for both the supercritical regime (p > n) yielding a single solution, and the critical regime (p = n) where uniqueness holds up to scaling.

title: A Massively Parallel Three-Grid Preconditioner for the High-Frequency Helmholtz Equation
summary: Accurate simulation of three-dimensional time-harmonic wave propagation over many wavelengths requires control of phase error and efficient solution of large indefinite systems. We develop a three-grid solver based on the compact 27-point interpolated optimized finite-difference (IOFD) discretization. Its wavenumber-dependent stencil supports a fine-grid resolution of six points per shortest wavelength and an unshifted physical correction on the \(2h\) grid at only three points per shortest wavelength. The method retains unshifted IOFD operators on the \(h\) and \(2h\) grids, while a complex-shifted \(2h\)--\(4h\) auxiliary cycle preconditions a factorization-free iterative approximation of the coarse inverse. Restricting the shift to this auxiliary cycle preserves the propagative character of the coarse correction. Comparison with the outgoing Green function confirms phase and relative-amplitude accuracy on a sequence of meshes up to \(6144^3\), with the largest problem spanning approximately 1024 wavelengths per coordinate. The same fixed solver configuration retains robust convergence across smooth, discontinuous, high-contrast, and geophysical velocity models and exhibits scalable parallel performance. In particular, a problem spanning approximately 340 wavelengths in each coordinate direction is solved in 18.1 seconds on just 64 NVIDIA A100 GPUs.

AI.tldr: A three-grid solver for large-scale 3D time-harmonic wave propagation using compact 27-point IOFD discretization, achieving high accuracy with complex-shifted auxiliary cycles and scalable performance on GPUs.
AI.motivation: Accurate simulation of 3D time-harmonic waves over many wavelengths demands precise phase-error control and efficient solution of large indefinite linear systems, which are computationally challenging.
AI.method: Develops a three-grid solver based on compact 27-point interpolated optimized finite-difference (IOFD) discretization. Uses wavenumber-dependent stencils at 6 points per wavelength on the fine grid, unshifted IOFD operators on h and 2h grids, and a complex-shifted 2h-4h auxiliary cycle to precondition the coarse inverse via factorization-free iterative approximation.
AI.result: Demonstrates phase and amplitude accuracy verified against outgoing Green functions on meshes up to 6144^3 (~1024 wavelengths per coordinate). Robust convergence across smooth, discontinuous, high-contrast, and geophysical models. A ~340-wavelength problem solves in 18.1 seconds on 64 NVIDIA A100 GPUs.
AI.conclusion: The proposed solver achieves scalable, robust, and highly accurate large-scale wave propagation simulation with excellent parallel performance, making it suitable for extreme-scale problems spanning hundreds of wavelengths.

title: Revealing Hidden Orbital Pathways in NonThermal Hot Carrier Relaxation of MXenes via Non-Secular Redfield Quantum Kinetic
summary: Nonthermal carrier relaxation is routinely inferred from population dynamics or spectroscopic observables, yet neither class of quantity uniquely identifies the microscopic channels through which energy and coherence are redistributed. We introduce a pathway-resolved quantum kinetic framework that simultaneously projects ultrafast relaxation onto orbital populations, inter-orbital energy fluxes, coherence, spectroscopic visibility, and a hidden-pathway sector of the dynamical transfer network. Application to MXenes exposes strongly nonuniform orbital redistribution together with material specific hierarchies of microscopic transfer channels. Temperature, excitation amplitude, and dissipative parameters modulate pathway competition and spectral amplitudes while leaving the identity of the dominant channels largely intact. Instantaneous energy flux, cumulative transfer, coherence, and spectroscopic visibility are shown to follow inequivalent hierarchical orderings. This nonequivalence isolates a set of hidden pathways that remain dynamically consequential despite weak conventional spectroscopic signatures. The resulting time energy coherence representation recasts nonthermal relaxation as a structured dynamical network comprising observable and hidden sectors, thereby providing a general methodology for resolving microscopic energy-transfer pathways in driven quantum materials.

AI.tldr: Introduces a pathway-resolved quantum kinetic framework that projects ultrafast nonthermal carrier relaxation onto orbital populations, energy fluxes, coherence, and spectroscopic visibility, revealing hidden dynamical transfer pathways in driven quantum materials like MXenes.
AI.motivation: Standard approaches infer nonthermal carrier relaxation from population dynamics or spectroscopic observables, but neither uniquely identifies the microscopic channels through which energy and coherence are redistributed.
AI.method: A pathway-resolved quantum kinetic framework that simultaneously projects ultrafast relaxation onto multiple observables: orbital populations, inter-orbital energy fluxes, coherence, spectroscopic visibility, and a hidden-pathway sector of the dynamical transfer network.
AI.result: Application to MXenes reveals strongly nonuniform orbital redistribution and material-specific hierarchies of microscopic transfer channels. Temperature, excitation amplitude, and dissipation modulate pathway competition and spectral amplitudes without changing dominant channel identity. Instantaneous energy flux, cumulative transfer, coherence, and spectroscopic visibility follow inequivalent hierarchical orderings, exposing hidden pathways that are dynamically consequential despite weak spectroscopic signatures.
AI.conclusion: The time-energy-coherence representation recasts nonthermal relaxation as a structured dynamical network with observable and hidden sectors, providing a general methodology for resolving microscopic energy-transfer pathways in driven quantum materials.

title: Classification of local $(-1)$-homogeneous axisymmetric solutions of the $3$D stationary Navier-Stokes equations with logarithmic singular-ray behavior
summary: We study the existence and classification of local $(-1)$-homogeneous axisymmetric solutions $(u, p)$ of the three-dimensional incompressible stationary Navier-Stokes equations near a singular ray. We focus on such solutions with Type II behavior, which satisfy $0<\limsup_{x\in\bS^2, x\to P}|u|/|\ln \text{dist}(x, P)|<\infty$, where $P$ is the south or north pole. Apart from the Landau solutions, these are the least singular nontrivial $(-1)$-homogeneous axisymmetric solutions. We construct a four-parameter family of local $(-1)$-homogeneous axisymmetric solutions with at most logarithmic growth near the singular ray and represent them as convergent series whose coefficients are determined recursively. Conversely, we prove that every local $(-1)$-homogeneous axisymmetric solution satisfying $|u|=o(\text{dist} (x, P)^{-1})$ as $x\to P$ on $\bS^2$ belongs to this family. In particular, this family contains Type II solutions with nonzero swirl, in contrast to the global $(-1)$-homogeneous axisymmetric Type II solutions in $\R^3\setminus\{x'=0\}$, which have no swirl. We also establish derivative estimates for the constructed solutions and identify the singular force generated by these solutions across the singular ray in the sense of distributions.

AI.tldr: This paper studies local (-1)-homogeneous axisymmetric solutions of the 3D stationary incompressible Navier-Stokes equations near a singular ray, focusing on Type II solutions with logarithmic growth. The authors construct a four-parameter family of such solutions with convergent series representations, prove converses that all solutions with growth below dist(x,P)^{-1} belong to this family, and show these include Type II solutions with nonzero swirl (unlike global solutions). They also establish derivative estimates and distributional singular forces.
AI.motivation: The study of singular solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations is fundamental to understanding potential blow-up and regularity issues. (-1)-homogeneous axisymmetric solutions near a singular ray represent candidate singularities, and Type II solutions (which are less singular than Landau solutions except for these) may help classify the possible local singularity structures. Understanding their existence, classification, and properties is essential for advancing the theory of singularities in fluid dynamics.
AI.method: The authors construct a four-parameter family of local (-1)-homogeneous axisymmetric solutions with at most logarithmic growth near the singular ray, represented as convergent series with coefficients determined recursively. They prove a converse classification theorem showing every local solution with |u|=o(dist(x,P)^{-1}) belongs to this family. They also derive derivative estimates for these solutions and compute the singular force they generate across the singular ray in the distributional sense.
AI.result: The paper establishes both existence (via explicit constructive series) and classification (via converse theorem) of local Type II (-1)-homogeneous axisymmetric solutions near a singular ray. A key finding is that this local family contains Type II solutions with nonzero swirl, contrasting with global (-1)-homogeneous axisymmetric Type II solutions in R^3\{x'=0}, which have no swirl. Derivative estimates and distributional singular forces are also computed.
AI.conclusion: The constructed four-parameter family completely classifies local (-1)-homogeneous axisymmetric solutions with less-than-(dist)^{-1} growth, providing a complete picture of Type II singular behavior near a singular ray in the stationary Navier-Stokes setting. The presence of swirling Type II solutions in the local setting but not global setting highlights significant differences between local and global singularity structures.

title: Why the Kellogg Mesh Is Radial: A Hidden Energy Symmetry
summary: Kellogg's checkerboard interface problem is a classical benchmark for robust adaptive finite element methods. Its successful adaptive meshes are radial: they refine strongly toward the interface crossing but show no angular structure, despite the large contrast and the asymmetric solution. We explain this by proving that the singular solution $u(r,θ)=r^γμ(θ)$ satisfies the exact identities $κ|\nabla u|^2=Λr^{2γ-2}$ and $κ|\nabla^2 u|_F^2=2(1-γ)^2Λr^{2γ-4}$, where $|\cdot|_F$ is the Frobenius norm, the Hessian is taken separately in each quadrant, and $Λ=γ^2\cos^2(πγ/4)$. The point is what has disappeared: the right-hand sides depend on $r$ alone, although $κ$ and $u$ each depend on the angle as well. Both identities extend across the interfaces, and the elements at the crossing point balance in the same way. Combined with the principle of equal discretization-error distribution, the identities show that the target element density is radial, so a correct mesh should display nothing but refinement toward the center. The familiar picture is therefore a spatial consequence of the coefficient-weighted requirement underlying robust error analysis, rather than a separate empirical fact. It is also what makes the benchmark readable by eye: a Kellogg mesh that is not radial is visible evidence that the computation is not following the coefficient-weighted local difficulty. The reading is specific to this benchmark; on a two-material problem whose weighted difficulty is not radial, the same robust estimator produces a strongly material-biased mesh.

AI.tldr: This paper explains why adaptive meshes for the Kellogg checkerboard benchmark are radial (refining only toward the interface crossing with no angular structure) by proving exact identities for the singular solution: κ|∇u|² = Λr^(2γ-2) and κ|∇²u|²_F = 2(1-γ)²Λr^(2γ-4), where the right-hand sides depend only on r, despite κ and u each depending on the angle. Combined with equal discretization-error distribution, this shows the target element density is radial, explaining the familiar meshing pattern as a mathematical consequence rather than an empirical accident.
AI.motivation: To explain a long-observed but unexplained phenomenon: why Kellogg's checkerboard benchmark produces purely radial adaptive meshes with no angular structure, despite large material contrast and asymmetric solution. The authors aim to prove this is a mathematical necessity from robust error analysis principles, not a coincidence.
AI.method: The authors prove exact analytical identities for the singular solution u(r,θ)=r^γ μ(θ): κ|∇u|² = Λr^(2γ-2) and κ|∇²u|²_F = 2(1-γ)²Λr^(2γ-4), where Λ = γ² cos²(πγ/4), and the Hessian is taken per quadrant. These identities show the coefficient-weighted difficulty depends only on the radius. They then combine these identities with the principle of equal discretization-error distribution to derive the target element density.
AI.result: The identities prove that although κ (coefficient) and u (solution) each depend on the angle θ, their product combination appearing in error analysis depends only on r. Combined with equal-error distribution principles, this shows the target element density is radial—explaining why correct Kellogg meshes show refinement only toward the center. The authors also demonstrate the reading is benchmark-specific: non-radial weighted difficulty in other two-material problems produces material-biased meshes.
AI.conclusion: The radial nature of Kellogg benchmark adaptive meshes is not an empirical accident but a mathematical consequence of the coefficient-weighted robust error estimation framework. A non-radial Kellogg mesh indicates the computation is not following coefficient-weighted local difficulty. This provides both theoretical understanding and a practical diagnostic for adaptive method correctness.

title: Roles of vortices and turbulent eddies in particle preferential concentration and deposition in the human respiratory tract
summary: Precise targeting of pharmaceutical aerosols is critical to the efficacy and safety of inhaled therapies. This study focused on the influences of vortices and turbulent eddies on preferential concentration and deposition of pharmaceutical aerosols within the human respiratory tract. By reconstructing a high-fidelity respiratory tract geometry spanning the nasal cavity down to sequential bronchi from computed tomography (CT) images and assigning physiologically realistic transient breathing profiles, an unsteady Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (URANS) framework using the shear stress transport (SST) k-w turbulence model and a stress-blended eddy simulation (SBES) framework of human respiratory tract were built. Beyond flow field analyses, Vorono diagrams and a set of newly-defined spatial accuracy metrics were adopted to quantitatively characterize particle distributions and localized prediction discrepancies. Spectral analysis revealed that the SBES simulations adequately recovered the prominent Kolmogorov -5/3 inertial scaling law. Such turbulent motion induces pronounced radial turbulent dispersion, forming particle clusters with higher cluster fractal dimensions D> 1.2 on the mid-plane of the laryngopharynx. Spatial accuracy metrics uncovered a critical dual deficiency of the URANS model: globally over-smears near-wall deposition by roughly 20%, simultaneously fails to resolve most high-concentration `hotspots' (the top 5% local extrema). These findings highlighted that the numerical resolution of transient vortices and turbulent eddies constitutes an indispensable prerequisite for accurately predicting of particle transport and deposition in the human respiratory tract.

AI.tldr: This study compares URANS and SBES turbulence modeling approaches for simulating pharmaceutical aerosol transport and deposition in a reconstructed human respiratory tract, revealing that URANS over-smears near-wall deposition by ~20% and fails to capture high-concentration hotspots, while SBES adequately resolves the Kolmogorov -5/3 inertial scaling law and turbulent-driven particle clustering.
AI.motivation: Precise targeting of pharmaceutical aerosols is critical for inhaled therapy efficacy and safety, yet accurate prediction of particle transport and deposition in the respiratory tract depends on resolving transient vortices and turbulent eddies, which remains a key numerical challenge.
AI.method: A high-fidelity respiratory tract geometry was reconstructed from CT images spanning the nasal cavity to sequential bronchi. Two CFD frameworks were built: URANS using SST k-w turbulence model and a stress-blended eddy simulation (SBES). Vorono diagrams and newly-defined spatial accuracy metrics were used to quantify particle distributions and localized prediction discrepancies, along with spectral analysis.
AI.result: SBES recovered the prominent Kolmogorov -5/3 inertial scaling law, producing particle clusters with fractal dimensions D>1.2 in the laryngopharynx due to radial turbulent dispersion. URANS globally over-smeared near-wall deposition by roughly 20% and failed to resolve most top-5% high-concentration hotspots.
AI.conclusion: Accurate numerical resolution of transient vortices and turbulent eddies is an indispensable prerequisite for reliable prediction of pharmaceutical aerosol transport and deposition in the human respiratory tract, demonstrating the superiority of scale-resolving simulations like SBES over URANS.

title: Singularity formation and self-shrinkers for the parabolic Bernoulli problem
summary: We study singularity formation for classical solutions of the parabolic Bernoulli free boundary problem and the associated self-similar profiles. Inspired by Ricci and mean curvature flows, we introduce a Type I assumption on the blow-up rate at a singular free boundary point, under which the parabolic rescalings are compact and every tangent flow is a non-trivial self-shrinking solution of the elliptic profile equation. The proof establishes convergence of the positivity sets and recovers the Bernoulli condition in the limit, despite the absence of a minimizing structure. In the subcritical regime, every tangent flow is a double plane. We next classify all radial self-shrinkers. Besides the known ball and exterior profiles, there is a unique annular profile. We obtain dimension-uniform bounds and sharp asymptotics for its inner and outer radii, including a quantitative outward bias of its midpoint. These delicate estimates yield a complete classification of the signs of the linear spectrum for the annular solution in every dimension. As a consequence, the ball is dynamically stable modulo ambient symmetries, whereas the annulus is dynamically unstable, with genuine unstable modes of angular degrees $0,1,2,3$. We finally prove, from the spectral nondegeneracy of the compact radial profiles, that whenever one tangent flow is a ball or an annular solution, the tangent flow is unique. One borderline spectral sign in dimensions $2\leq n \leq 4000$ is verified by a rigorous computer-assisted argument using interval arithmetic.

AI.tldr: This paper studies singularity formation in the parabolic Bernoulli free boundary problem, introducing a Type I blow-up assumption. It proves compactness of parabolic rescalings, classifies self-shrinking profiles (ball, exterior, and a unique annular solution), establishes stability of the ball and instability of the annulus via linear spectral analysis, and proves uniqueness of tangent flows from spectral nondegeneracy.
AI.motivation: To understand singularity formation in the parabolic Bernoulli free boundary problem by establishing structural results analogous to those in Ricci and mean curvature flows, including a Type I assumption for compactness and characterization of tangent flows.
AI.method: Introduces a Type I blow-up rate assumption; applies parabolic rescaling compactness arguments to obtain tangent flows as self-shrinking solutions; classifies all radial self-shrinkers (ball, exterior, annular); computes dimension-uniform bounds and sharp asymptotics for the annulus; performs complete linear spectral analysis for stability; uses interval arithmetic computer-assisted verification for one borderline spectral sign in dimensions 2≤n≤4000.
AI.result: Every tangent flow is a self-shrinking solution (double plane in subcritical regime); radial self-shrinkers are classified (ball, exterior, unique annulus); the ball is dynamically stable while the annulus is dynamically unstable with unstable modes of angular degrees 0,1,2,3; tangent flows are unique whenever a ball or annular solution appears; borderline spectral sign verified rigorously by computer-assisted argument.
AI.conclusion: The Type I assumption framework yields a complete structural understanding of singularities in the parabolic Bernoulli problem, with a full classification of radial self-shrinkers, stability/instability results, and tangent flow uniqueness, including a computer-verified borderline case.

title: The longest-edge bisection algorithm may produce degenerating tetrahedra
summary: An explicit sequence of tetrahedra generated by the longest-edge bisection algorithm is shown to degenerate. The example violates shape regularity and both the minimum- and maximum-angle conditions, demonstrating that arbitrary tie-breaking among longest edges does not guarantee nondegeneration.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an explicit example of a tetrahedron sequence generated by the longest-edge bisection algorithm that degenerates, showing that arbitrary tie-breaking among longest edges can lead to shape degradation.
AI.motivation: The longest-edge bisection algorithm is widely used in mesh refinement, and it is important to understand whether the choice of which longest edge to bisect (when multiple longest edges exist) affects the quality of the resulting meshes. This paper aims to show that arbitrary tie-breaking can lead to degeneration.
AI.method: The authors construct an explicit counterexample: a sequence of tetrahedra produced by the longest-edge bisection algorithm that degenerates. They analyze the sequence and demonstrate that it violates shape regularity, the minimum-angle condition, and the maximum-angle condition.
AI.result: An explicit family of tetrahedra generated by longest-edge bisection is shown to degenerate, serving as a counterexample to the belief that arbitrary tie-breaking among longest edges preserves nondegeneration.
AI.conclusion: Arbitrary tie-breaking among longest edges in the longest-edge bisection algorithm does not guarantee nondegeneration of the resulting tetrahedra, as demonstrated by an explicit degenerating sequence.

title: Emergent Noncollinearity and Near-Degenerate Magnetic Superlattices in AT6X6 Kagome Metals
summary: Ferromagnetic AT6X6 Kagome compounds are a popular class of systems in which quantum magnetism with topological features has been observed. These systems allow easy chemical substitution, creating an opportunity to fine-tune their properties. In this paper, we present electronic-structure and magnetic ground-state studies of several AT6X6 compounds with relatively low magnetic-ground-state stability. We find unusual magnetic orderings, including complex spin-spiral states and the formation of magnetic long-range superstructures. While LiFe6Ga6 and TiMn6Ge6 retain collinear AFM ground states with low-energy FM/AFM layer sequences, competing spin-spiral and long-period antiferromagnetic structures in MgFe6Ga6 and a double-spin-spiral ground state in TiFe6Ga6 were determined. Magnetism in all these systems appears local, with adiabatic energy profiles suggesting non-Heisenberg long-range interactions, including a strong biquadratic term. In TiMn6Ge6, we found the conditions for magnetic tunneling. Our results show that, in addition to traditional magnetic topological features in such FM Kagome systems, near-degenerate magnetic superstructures suitable for spintronic switching applications can form naturally. Overall, these systems represent a potentially rich playground for neutron diffraction and spintronics experimental studies.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates the electronic structure and magnetic ground states of several AT6X6 Kagome compounds with low magnetic ground-state stability, revealing unusual magnetic orderings including spin-spiral states, long-range magnetic superstructures, and a double-spin-spiral ground state. These systems exhibit local magnetism with non-Heisenberg long-range interactions including strong biquadratic coupling, and some display conditions for magnetic tunneling. The authors suggest these near-degenerate magnetic superstructures could be useful for spintronic switching applications.
AI.motivation: Ferromagnetic AT6X6 Kagome compounds are of interest due to quantum magnetism with topological features. These systems allow easy chemical substitution for property tuning, and the authors aim to explore compounds with relatively low magnetic-ground-state stability to discover unusual magnetic orderings and potential spintronic applications.
AI.method: The authors performed electronic-structure calculations and magnetic ground-state studies on several AT6X6 compounds, including determining adiabatic energy profiles to characterize magnetic interactions and ground-state magnetic orderings.
AI.result: The study found unusual magnetic orderings: collinear AFM ground states with low-energy FM/AFM layer sequences in LiFe6Ga6 and TiMn6Ge6; competing spin-spiral and long-period antiferromagnetic structures in MgFe6Ga6; and a double-spin-spiral ground state in TiFe6Ga6. Magnetism is local with non-Heisenberg long-range interactions, including a strong biquadratic term, and magnetic tunneling conditions were found in TiMn6Ge6.
AI.conclusion: Beyond traditional magnetic topological features in FM Kagome systems, near-degenerate magnetic superstructures suitable for spintronic switching can form naturally in these compounds. These systems represent a promising playground for neutron diffraction and spintronics experimental studies.

title: Uniqueness for the spatially homogeneous Boltzmann equation in critical Sobolev spaces
summary: We study the spatially homogeneous Boltzmann equation without angular cutoff for very soft potentials satisfying the inverse power law relation $γ+4s=1$. Our main results establish the existence, uniqueness, stability and regularization estimates of solutions in the critical Sobolev space $ H^{-(γ+ 2s + \frac{3}{2})} $ with a logarithmic correction. Combined with the recently established monotonicity of the Fisher information, the solutions extend globally in time. Our primary tools are energy estimates based on a simultaneous dyadic localization in the phase and frequency variables, together with sharp commutator estimates between the collision operator and the localization operators.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes well-posedness (existence, uniqueness, stability) and regularization estimates for the spatially homogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann equation with very soft potentials satisfying γ+4s=1, working in a critical Sobolev space with logarithmic correction. Combined with Fisher information monotonicity, global-in-time extension of solutions is achieved using energy estimates with simultaneous dyadic localization in phase and frequency, plus sharp commutator estimates.
AI.motivation: The very soft potentials case (γ+4s=1) is the most challenging regime for the non-cutoff Boltzmann equation, where the collision operator's coercivity is weak and classical well-posedness theories fail. Establishing a critical well-posedness theory in the sharp Sobolev space is a fundamental open problem that bridges harmonic analysis and kinetic theory.
AI.method: The authors employ energy estimates based on simultaneous dyadic localization in both the phase (spatial) and frequency variables, combined with sharp commutator estimates between the collision operator and the localization operators. This approach captures the anisotropic nature of the collision operator in the very soft potential regime. They also leverage the recently established monotonicity of Fisher information to extend solutions globally in time.
AI.result: The main results are: (1) existence, uniqueness, and stability of solutions in the critical Sobolev space H^{-(γ+2s+3/2)} with a logarithmic correction, and (2) global-in-time extension of solutions via Fisher information monotonicity.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a complete well-posedness theory in the critical regularity space for the very soft potentials case of the non-cutoff Boltzmann equation, resolving a key difficulty in the borderline regime γ+4s=1 and enabling global solutions through novel phase-frequency localization techniques.

title: Transform-Based Multilinear Algebra via Tensor Decomposition
summary: Transform-based tensor products, including the T-product and its more general form, namely the higher-order tensor-tensor product, have become fundamental tools for multilinear data analysis in applications such as image processing, signal reconstruction, and robotics. While invertible transforms enable tensor computations to be carried out via matrix operations in the transform domain, the resulting storage and computational costs remain prohibitive for high-dimensional, higher-order tensors. To address this challenge, we integrate low-rank tensor decomposition techniques, specifically tensor train decomposition (TTD) and hierarchical Tucker decomposition (HTD), into transform-based multilinear algebra to improve computational and memory efficiency. In particular, we develop TTD- and HTD-based formulations for the T-product and its associated key algebra, such as block diagonalization and tensor singular value decomposition, by operating directly on the factor matrices or tensors of the decompositions. The framework is further generalized to the higher-order tensor-tensor product and applied to multilinear model order reduction problems. We demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our framework with numerical examples.

AI.tldr: This paper integrates low-rank tensor decompositions (TTD and HTD) into transform-based tensor products (T-product and higher-order tensor-tensor product) to reduce the prohibitive storage and computational costs for high-dimensional, higher-order tensors, and applies the framework to multilinear model order reduction.
AI.motivation: Transform-based tensor products are fundamental for multilinear data analysis, but their storage and computational costs become prohibitive for high-dimensional, higher-order tensors when operations are carried out via matrix operations in the transform domain.
AI.method: The authors integrate tensor train decomposition (TTD) and hierarchical Tucker decomposition (HTD) into transform-based multilinear algebra. They develop TTD- and HTD-based formulations for the T-product and its key algebraic operations (block diagonalization and tensor singular value decomposition) by operating directly on the factor matrices or tensors of the decompositions. The framework is then generalized to the higher-order tensor-tensor product.
AI.result: The framework demonstrates effectiveness and efficiency through numerical examples, applied to multilinear model order reduction problems.
AI.conclusion: Combining low-rank tensor decomposition techniques with transform-based multilinear algebra significantly improves computational and memory efficiency for high-dimensional, higher-order tensor operations.

title: Riesz Energy Subset Selection in the Euclidean Plane is NP-Hard
comment: Keywords: Riesz energy, subset selection, NP-completeness, geometric optimization, planar cubic graphs, independent set, Ising model, computational geometry
summary: We prove that minimum Riesz $s$-energy subset selection in the Euclidean plane is NP-complete already for the fixed exponent $s=2$. To our knowledge, this is the first Euclidean hardness result for exact Riesz-energy subset selection in which both the ambient dimension and the exponent are fixed. The reduction uses Barahona's planar cubic Ising model with uniform field. A spin is encoded by one diagonal of a four-point square. Axis-aligned selector chains implement ferromagnetic consistency, while a $45^\circ$ terminal geometry yields an antiferromagnetic source interaction. Rational diagonal perturbations realize the magnetic field, and all remaining interactions are dominated by polynomial separation. Because $s=2$ and all coordinates are rational, every constructed energy and the decision threshold are rational exactly.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that minimum Riesz s-energy subset selection in the Euclidean plane is NP-complete even when the exponent is fixed at s=2, marking the first Euclidean hardness result where both ambient dimension and exponent are fixed. The proof reduces Barahona's planar cubic Ising model with uniform field to the Riesz energy problem using geometric constructions with rational coordinates.
AI.motivation: To establish computational hardness for exact Riesz-energy subset selection in a fixed Euclidean setting, where previous results required variable dimension or exponent. This closes a gap regarding whether the problem remains tractable in fixed dimension with fixed exponent.
AI.method: The reduction encodes Barahona's planar cubic Ising model with uniform field. Spins are represented by diagonals of four-point squares, ferromagnetic consistency is enforced via axis-aligned selector chains, antiferromagnetic interactions arise from a 45° terminal geometry, and rational diagonal perturbations encode the magnetic field. All non-essential interactions are separated polynomially to dominate the energy terms.
AI.result: Minimum Riesz s-energy subset selection is NP-complete for s=2 in the Euclidean plane. Since s=2 and all coordinates are rational, all constructed energies and the decision threshold are exactly rational.
AI.conclusion: The result establishes the first Euclidean hardness proof for exact Riesz-energy subset selection with both fixed ambient dimension and fixed exponent, and the rational-exactness ensures robust complexity classification.

title: The Monge--Ampère equation on graphs
summary: We introduce a version of the Monge--Ampère equation on finite graphs, motivated by nonlinear graph-based interpolation and semi-supervised learning. The operator is defined as the product of discrete analogs of the Hessian eigenvalues, obtained via local order statistics of function values at neighboring vertices. We derive an equivalent Bellman-type formulation of the inhomogeneous Dirichlet problem, establish a comparison principle and uniqueness in the strictly graph-convex class, and investigate existence via Perron's method, identifying certain graph-theoretic obstructions. We also study the homogeneous equation, for which the problem reduces to a nonlinear interpolation rule involving the smallest discrete eigenvalue. Finally, we propose numerical schemes for both the homogeneous and inhomogeneous problems.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a Monge-Ampère type equation on finite graphs, motivated by nonlinear graph-based interpolation and semi-supervised learning. The operator uses products of discrete Hessian eigenvalue analogs derived from local order statistics. The authors establish a Bellman-type formulation, comparison principle, uniqueness in strictly graph-convex classes, existence via Perron's method (with graph-theoretic obstructions noted), study the homogeneous case as a nonlinear interpolation rule, and propose numerical schemes.
AI.motivation: To extend the Monge-Ampère equation, a well-studied PDE, to discrete graph settings for applications in nonlinear interpolation and semi-supervised learning on graphs.
AI.method: Defines a discrete Monge-Ampère operator using products of discrete Hessian eigenvalue analogs from local order statistics. Derives an equivalent Bellman-type formulation, applies Perron's method for existence, and develops numerical schemes for both homogeneous and inhomogeneous problems.
AI.result: Establishes a comparison principle and uniqueness in the strictly graph-convex class; identifies graph-theoretic obstructions to existence; shows the homogeneous equation reduces to a nonlinear interpolation rule involving the smallest discrete eigenvalue; provides numerical schemes.
AI.conclusion: A discrete Monge-Ampère equation is viable on finite graphs with theoretical guarantees (comparison principle, uniqueness, partial existence) and practical numerical solvers for interpolative applications.

title: Inertial Manifold Neural Operator for Dissipative Time-Dependent Partial Differential Equations
summary: In this paper, we introduce the Inertial Manifold Neural Operator (IMNO) for solving dissipative time-dependent partial differential equations (PDEs). The long-time dynamics of such systems often exhibit an effective low-dimensional structure due to dissipation. Unlike standard neural operator architectures such as the Fourier Neural Operator (FNO), IMNO explicitly leverages the low-dimensional structure to achieve better physical interpretability, accuracy, and stability in long-horizon autoregressive training and prediction for nonlinear dissipative PDEs. For shift-equivariant PDEs, we further introduce a shift-equivariant variant (IMNO-SE) of the proposed neural operator, ensuring that a spatial shift in the input induces the same spatial shift in the output. This symmetry-preserving inductive bias substantially improves its performance in shift-equivariant PDEs. Extensive benchmark experiments are presented to evaluate IMNO's performance numerically.

AI.tldr: Introduces the Inertial Manifold Neural Operator (IMNO) for solving dissipative time-dependent PDEs, leveraging the low-dimensional inertial manifold structure to improve interpretability, accuracy, and stability in long-horizon training. A shift-equivariant variant (IMNO-SE) is also proposed for shift-equivariant PDEs.
AI.motivation: Long-time dynamics of dissipative PDEs exhibit effective low-dimensional structure, but standard neural operators like FNO do not explicitly exploit this structure, limiting physical interpretability and stability in long-horizon autoregressive prediction.
AI.method: IMNO explicitly incorporates the inertial manifold (low-dimensional) structure into the neural operator architecture. For shift-equivariant PDEs, a symmetry-preserving variant IMNO-SE is introduced that ensures spatial shift equivariance between input and output.
AI.result: IMNO demonstrates better accuracy, physical interpretability, and stability in long-horizon autoregressive training and prediction for nonlinear dissipative PDEs. IMNO-SE substantially improves performance on shift-equivariant PDEs through its symmetry-preserving inductive bias.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly leveraging the inertial manifold structure in neural operator design yields superior performance for dissipative PDEs, and preserving symmetries further enhances results for shift-equivariant systems.

title: Kinetics of an Expanding Bacterial Colony: Continuum Modeling and Analysis
summary: We study the spatiotemporal dynamics of the expansion of a bacterial colony on a hard substrate. Nutrient from the substrate diffuses into the colony and is taken up by the bacterial cells for them to grow and divide, expanding the initial monolayer and then pancake-shaped colony. The concentration of nutrient determines the local cell growth rate in the colony. Mass conservation relates such local growth rate with velocity which is approximated to be proportional to the pressure gradient by Darcy's law. Altogether, the growing colony is modeled as a moving-boundary problem with the nutrient concentration and pressure solving a reaction-diffusion equation and Laplace's equation, respectively. We analyze the self-consistent moving-boundary model with respect to different geometrical setting. For a general three-dimensional cylindrically symmetric model, we study the steady-state nutrient concentration. We construct and analyze a one-dimensional model for vertical expansion and a two-dimensional disk model for radial expansion of the colony. Our analysis finds that the nutrient depletes into the colony and slows down the vertical expansion of the colony. The vertical level where the nutrient concentration reaches the Monod constant, a threshold below which individual bacteria hardly grow, lowers down exponentially fast. We also estimate the asymptotic radial expansion rate. Moreover, we establish that the region where the nutrient concentration is above the threshold, allowing bacteria to grow and the colony to expand radially, is a ring-shaped peripheral region of fixed thickness. All these are consistent with experiment and agent-based simulations reported in literature.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a moving-boundary continuum model for bacterial colony expansion on a hard substrate, combining reaction-diffusion dynamics of nutrients with Darcy's law pressure-driven growth. The model predicts nutrient depletion into the colony, exponentially slowing vertical expansion, and identifies a fixed-thickness peripheral ring where nutrients exceed the Monod threshold, enabling radial expansion—all consistent with experiments and agent-based simulations.
AI.motivation: The authors seek to understand the spatiotemporal dynamics of bacterial colony expansion on hard substrates through a self-consistent mathematical model, bridging nutrient diffusion, cell growth, and mechanical expansion via moving-boundary formalism, and to verify these predictions against existing experimental and simulation data.
AI.method: The colony is modeled as a moving-boundary problem where nutrient concentration solves a reaction-diffusion equation and pressure satisfies Laplace's equation, with local growth rate governed by nutrient concentration (Monod-type kinetics) and velocity proportional to pressure gradient via Darcy's law. The authors analyze three geometrical settings: a general 3D cylindrically symmetric model for steady-state nutrient concentration, a 1D model for vertical expansion, and a 2D disk model for radial expansion.
AI.result: The analysis reveals that nutrient depletion into the colony causes the vertical expansion to slow down, with the level where nutrient concentration equals the Monod constant decaying exponentially fast. The radial expansion rate is asymptotically estimated, and the growth-permitting region (where nutrient exceeds threshold) is shown to be a peripheral ring of fixed thickness.
AI.conclusion: The moving-boundary model successfully captures key features of bacterial colony expansion, including exponentially slowing vertical growth due to nutrient depletion and a fixed-thickness peripheral growth ring for radial expansion, all consistent with experimental observations and agent-based simulations in the literature.

title: Data-Driven Dynamic Algorithm Dispatch with Large Language Models
comment: 3 pages, 2 figures. Accepted at the 2025 IEEE High Performance Extreme Computing Conference (HPEC). Outstanding Short Paper Award
summary: We introduce a large language model (LLM)-driven approach for generating dynamic algorithmic dispatch heuristics in high-performance linear algebra. By combining prompt engineering with LLaMA 3 and a curated performance database, the model learns to synthesize selection heuristics that exploit structural patterns to identify fast algorithmic choices. A case study on LU factorization demonstrates the model's ability to replicate expert-designed strategies. This work, developed as part of the DARPA-MIT SmartSolve project, highlights the promise of LLMs for algorithmic discovery and the development of more adaptive, fast linear algebra software.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an LLM-driven approach (using LLaMA 3 and prompt engineering) to generate dynamic algorithmic dispatch heuristics for high-performance linear algebra, demonstrated through a case study on LU factorization as part of the DARPA-MIT SmartSolve project.
AI.motivation: High-performance linear algebra requires selecting fast algorithmic choices based on structural patterns, but designing these dispatch heuristics by hand is difficult and non-adaptive. The authors motivate using LLMs to automate and improve this algorithmic discovery process.
AI.method: The approach combines prompt engineering with LLaMA 3 and a curated performance database. The LLM learns to synthesize selection heuristics that exploit structural patterns to identify fast algorithmic choices for linear algebra operations.
AI.result: A case study on LU factorization demonstrates the model's ability to replicate expert-designed dispatch strategies, showing the viability of LLM-generated heuristics.
AI.conclusion: The work highlights the promise of LLMs for algorithmic discovery and paves the way for more adaptive, fast linear algebra software.

title: Weak flocking for phase-spatially extended kinetic Cucker-Smale equation in a confining force field
summary: We study the quantitative fast and slow weak flocking of the phase-spatially extended kinetic Cucker-Smale model in confining potential fields. The confining potential is allowed to be nonconvex. In contrast to the phase-spatially confined case, the communication weight may have no positive lower bounds, while spatial and velocity diameters may remain infinite. Moreover, an indefinite Hessian of confining potential prevents the direct use of convexity-based coercive estimates. To overcome these difficulties, we identify three structural assumptions that are sufficient for the noncompact hypocoercive method: quadratic confinement, a globally Lipschitz force, and a strict virial inequality. The admissible class of confining potentials includes genuinely nonconvex radially symmetric ones and localized oscillatory perturbations of the harmonic potential. Weak flocking analysis combines three key ingredients: a microscopic mechanical-energy estimate, a time-varying effective region, and a macroscopic Lyapunov functional. For this, we first establish global existence for initial data with finite second moments. In the exponential mechanical-energy class, we further show the uniqueness and finite-time Osgood-type stability in 1-Wasserstein distance. For polynomially decaying initial mechanical-energy tails, we derive the optimal algebraic decay exponent of the fluctuation energy throughout the admissible communication-decay regime. The optimality is verified by a symmetric countably infinite particle solution for a fixed nonconvex potential. For exponentially decaying tails, a two-stage localization argument yields exponential weak flocking on an optimal exponential time scale. These results show that well-posedness and weak flocking persist even for fully noncompact data under genuinely nonconvex confining forces.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the quantitative fast and slow weak flocking behavior of the phase-spatially extended kinetic Cucker-Smale model under confining potential fields, including nonconvex potentials that lack positive lower bounds on communication weights and allow infinite spatial/velocity diameters.
AI.motivation: Previous analyses of the kinetic Cucker-Smale model relied on convexity-based coercive estimates and compact phase-space assumptions. Nonconvex confining potentials and fully noncompact data present fundamental difficulties that prevent direct application of existing methods, motivating the need for a new framework.
AI.method: The authors identify three structural assumptions—quadratic confinement, a globally Lipschitz force, and a strict virial inequality—sufficient for the noncompact hypocoercive method. They combine a microscopic mechanical-energy estimate, a time-varying effective region, and a macroscopic Lyapunov functional to analyze weak flocking. They also employ a two-stage localization argument for exponential decay cases.
AI.result: Global existence is established for initial data with finite second moments. Uniqueness and finite-time Osgood-type stability in 1-Wasserstein distance hold in the exponential mechanical-energy class. Optimal algebraic decay exponents are derived for polynomially decaying tails, verified by a symmetric countably infinite particle solution. Exponential weak flocking on an optimal exponential time scale is obtained for exponentially decaying tails.
AI.conclusion: Well-posedness and weak flocking persist even for fully noncompact data under genuinely nonconvex confining forces, extending the applicability of the kinetic Cucker-Smale model analysis to a much broader class of confining potentials.

title: Rapid Earthquake-to-Tsunami Waveform Generation via Large-Scale Multi-GPU FFT Convolution Applied to the Cascadia Subduction Zone
summary: Data-driven methods for earthquake and tsunami early warning rely on large ensembles of rupture scenarios and their resulting waveforms, but generating such datasets with repeated high-fidelity seismic and tsunami simulations is prohibitively expensive. We exploit the linear time-invariant structure of both dynamics to precompute elastic Green's functions and acoustic-gravity adjoint responses, reducing the source-to-waveform map to two consecutive convolution operators. We evaluate these convolutions with a distributed, FFT-accelerated GPU pipeline that partitions the large seafloor grid across GPUs and directly generates the final observation waveforms. We demonstrate the scalability of this pipeline for the Cascadia Subduction Zone with 963 subfaults, 2,416,530 seafloor grid points, 64 observation locations, and 256 timesteps, requiring 9.45 TiB of aggregate GPU memory.
