A notable feature of our analysis is that this method can be applied even when the rarefaction wave has large amplitude. In particular, this resolves, in a generic setting, the open problem of the stability of inflow wave patterns containing a viscous shock for Navier--Stokes--Fourier system.

AI.tldr: The paper proves time-asymptotic stability of solutions to the inflow problem for the one-dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier system on a half-line, showing convergence to a superposition of a degenerate boundary layer, rarefaction wave, viscous contact wave, and viscous shock. The rarefaction wave can have arbitrarily large strength, and the method of a-contraction with shifts is used to control the viscous shock.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to resolve a long-standing open problem: proving the stability of inflow wave patterns containing a viscous shock for the Navier-Stokes-Fourier system. Previous results did not cover the most generic wave pattern combining all relevant waves, particularly when a viscous shock is present alongside a large-amplitude rarefaction wave.
AI.method: The authors employ the method of a-contraction with shifts to control the viscous shock. They consider the most generic wave pattern (superposition of a degenerate boundary layer, rarefaction, viscous contact wave, and viscous shock) and assume small boundary-layer, contact-wave, and shock strengths, while allowing arbitrarily large rarefaction-wave strength. The proof establishes convergence up to a time-dependent shift for the shock component.
AI.result: The solution to the inflow problem converges time-asymptotically to the corresponding superposition of waves, with the rarefaction wave allowed to have arbitrarily large strength and the viscous shock controlled via time-dependent shifts. This resolves the open problem of stability of inflow wave patterns containing a viscous shock for the Navier-Stokes-Fourier system.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes, in a generic setting, the time-asymptotic stability of the most complex wave pattern for the inflow problem of the Navier-Stokes-Fourier system, demonstrating that the a-contraction method can be extended to handle large-amplitude rarefaction waves in the presence of viscous shocks.

title: Interior Hessian estimates for the quadratic Hessian equation
summary: We establish interior Hessian estimates and smoothness for viscosity solutions of the quadratic Hessian equation on the positive branch in arbitrary dimension.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes interior Hessian estimates and smoothness results for viscosity solutions of the quadratic Hessian equation on the positive branch, valid in arbitrary dimension.
AI.motivation: The quadratic Hessian equation presents significant challenges due to its structure, and establishing regularity results (particularly Hessian estimates and smoothness) for viscosity solutions is a fundamental question that was previously unresolved in general dimensions on the positive branch.
AI.method: The paper develops interior Hessian estimates and proves smoothness for viscosity solutions of the quadratic Hessian equation, specifically working on the positive branch in arbitrary dimension.
AI.result: Interior Hessian estimates are established and smoothness of viscosity solutions is proven for the quadratic Hessian equation on the positive branch in arbitrary dimension.
AI.conclusion: The authors resolve the regularity question for viscosity solutions of the quadratic Hessian equation on the positive branch, showing that these solutions are smooth in any dimension.

title: The parabolic Dini-$β$ condition and absolute continuity of surface and caloric measure
summary:
We show if $\partial Ω$ is the graph of a parabolic Lipschitz function, then parabolic surface measure $σ$ of $\partial Ω$ is absolutely continuous with respect to its caloric measure if and only if a (square) Dini-$β$ condition is satisfied. More specifically, the (square) Dini-$β$ condition is that \[\int_0^1 \hatβ(X,t,r)^2 \frac{dr}{r} < \infty, \quad \text{$σ$-a.e. } (X,t) \in \partial Ω.\] Here $\hatβ$ is a parabolic version of the Jones ($L^2$) $β$-numbers. We show that these conditions are satisfied if and only if the graph is covered by a countable collection of {\it regular} Lipschitz graphs, that is, graphs with additional in-time regularity in the form of a half order time derivative in the parabolic BMO space. This supports the view that covering by {\it regular} Lipschitz graphs is the right notion for qualitative parabolic rectifiability in the context of parabolic PDEs.
  We also show that if \[\int_0^1 \hatβ(X,t,r)^2 \frac{dr}{r} < \infty\] up to a set of caloric measure zero then the caloric measure is absolutely continuous with respect to surface measure.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes that for domains whose boundary is the graph of a parabolic Lipschitz function, parabolic surface measure is absolutely continuous with respect to caloric measure if and only if a square Dini-β condition holds (involving parabolic Jones β-numbers). This condition is further shown to be equivalent to the boundary being coverable by countably many regular Lipschitz graphs with half-order time derivatives in parabolic BMO space, supporting this as the right notion of qualitative parabolic rectifiability for parabolic PDEs.
AI.motivation: To characterize when caloric measure and surface measure are mutually absolutely continuous for parabolic Lipschitz domains, and to identify the correct notion of parabolic rectifiability in the context of parabolic PDEs — analogous to how Dini conditions and β-numbers characterize absolute continuity in the elliptic setting.
AI.method: The paper uses parabolic Jones (L²) β-numbers to define a square Dini-β condition. It proves equivalence between: (1) the square Dini-β condition holding σ-a.e., (2) absolute continuity of caloric measure with respect to surface measure, and (3) covering of the boundary by countable collections of regular Lipschitz graphs (having half-order time derivatives in parabolic BMO). A second result shows the square Dini-β condition up to a set of caloric measure zero is sufficient for absolute continuity of caloric measure with respect to surface measure.
AI.result: The square Dini-β condition (involving parabolic β-numbers) holds σ-a.e. if and only if caloric measure is absolutely continuous with respect to parabolic surface measure, which is also equivalent to countable covering by regular Lipschitz graphs. Additionally, the square Dini-β condition holding up to caloric measure zero implies absolute continuity of caloric measure with respect to surface measure.
AI.conclusion: The paper validates that covering by regular Lipschitz graphs (with half-order time regularity in parabolic BMO) is the appropriate notion of qualitative parabolic rectifiability for parabolic PDE contexts, as it precisely captures the absolute continuity relationship between caloric and surface measures.

title: Analyticity of the data-to-solution map for a stationary Navier-Stokes fluid-structure interaction problem
summary: We consider a stationary fluid--structure interaction problem in which the steady Navier--Stokes equations are coupled, through a free elastic interface, with a clamped Euler-Bernoulli beam equation. Using a complexification of the fixed-domain formulation and the holomorphic implicit function theorem, we prove that, in a neighbourhood of the trivial solution, the mapping from the right-hand side to the weak solution is real analytic. As a byproduct we obtain a small-data existence and local uniqueness result for the coupled system. Our motivation comes from data-driven reduced-order modelling for parametric PDEs, where approximation properties are closely related to the regularity of the solution map. Numerically, a manufactured-solution test exhibits approximately second-order convergence in the reported relative $L^2$ errors, while a proper orthogonal decomposition study for a parametric force family shows rapid decay of the empirical reconstruction error until a numerical floor is reached.

AI.tldr: The paper proves that the solution map of a stationary fluid-structure interaction problem (Navier-Stokes coupled with an Euler-Bernoulli beam via a free elastic interface) is real analytic near the trivial solution, using complexification and the holomorphic implicit function theorem. This yields small-data existence and local uniqueness, with numerical tests showing second-order convergence and rapid POD error decay.
AI.motivation: The work is motivated by data-driven reduced-order modelling for parametric PDEs, where the regularity (analyticity) of the solution map directly impacts approximation properties of reduced-order models.
AI.method: The authors employ a complexification of the fixed-domain formulation and apply the holomorphic implicit function theorem to establish real analyticity of the mapping from the right-hand side to the weak solution near the trivial solution.
AI.result: They prove the solution map is real analytic in a neighbourhood of the trivial solution, obtaining small-data existence and local uniqueness as a byproduct. Numerically, a manufactured-solution test shows approximately second-order convergence in relative L2 errors, and a proper orthogonal decomposition study for parametric forces shows rapid decay of empirical reconstruction error until reaching a numerical floor.
AI.conclusion: Analytic regularity of the solution map for the fluid-structure interaction problem is established, supporting the theoretical foundation for efficient reduced-order modelling of this parametric PDE system.

title: Quasiconvexity of the Burkholder function on symmetric matrices
summary: We use Morse Theory to prove that the Burkholder function is quasiconvex on symmetric matrices, which implies several sharp inequalities for the Beurling--Ahlfors transform when acting on real-valued functions. More generally, we prove that the separating functions introduced by Székelyhidi are quasiconvex on symmetric matrices.

AI.tldr: The paper uses Morse Theory to prove that the Burkholder function and Székelyhidi's separating functions are quasiconvex on symmetric matrices, leading to sharp inequalities for the Beurling–Ahlfors transform on real-valued functions.
AI.motivation: The Burkholder function and separating functions are central to establishing sharp estimates for singular integral operators like the Beurling–Ahlfors transform. Proving their quasiconvexity is a key step, and Morse Theory provides a novel tool to establish this property.
AI.method: The authors employ Morse Theory to analyze the level sets and critical points of the Burkholder function on the space of symmetric matrices, demonstrating quasiconvexity. The same approach is extended to the more general separating functions introduced by Székelyhidi.
AI.result: The Burkholder function is proven to be quasiconvex on symmetric matrices, and similarly for Székelyhidi's separating functions. This yields several sharp inequalities for the Beurling–Ahlfors transform acting on real-valued functions.
AI.conclusion: Quasiconvexity of these key functions is rigorously established via Morse Theory, providing a new proof framework and enabling sharp inequalities for the Beurling–Ahlfors transform.

title: Geometric desingularisation of the sharp-to-smooth travelling wave transition
summary: We study travelling front solutions of a family of degenerate Fisher-KPP equations $u_t=(u^n u_x)_x+u(1-u^n)$, where $n$ is a positive integer. At the minimal wave speed $c_{\rm min}=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{1+n}}$, these equations admit sharp front solutions, corresponding to an explicit heteroclinic orbit in the travelling wave phase-space. We show how this sharp front is perturbed when the wave speed is increased to $c=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{1+n}}+\varepsilon$, with $\varepsilon$ sufficiently small. We use a well-motivated geometric desingularisation (also known as blow-up) near the degenerate equilibrium at the leading edge. By analysing the resulting directional and rescaling charts, we construct a singular heteroclinic orbit connecting the relevant asymptotic states, providing a simple geometric proof of the transition from sharp to smooth travelling fronts.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes travelling front solutions of degenerate Fisher-KPP equations, showing how sharp fronts (at minimal wave speed) transition to smooth fronts when the wave speed is slightly increased, using geometric desingularization (blow-up) techniques to construct a singular heteroclinic orbit connecting the relevant asymptotic states.
AI.motivation: To understand how sharp travelling front solutions of degenerate Fisher-KPP equations behave when the wave speed exceeds the minimal speed, and to provide a geometric proof of the transition from sharp to smooth fronts.
AI.method: Geometric desingularization (blow-up) near the degenerate equilibrium at the leading edge of the travelling wave, combined with analysis of directional and rescaling charts to construct a singular heteroclinic orbit.
AI.result: A simple geometric proof of the transition from sharp to smooth travelling fronts for wave speeds slightly above the minimal speed, via construction of a singular heteroclinic orbit connecting the relevant asymptotic states.
AI.conclusion: The blow-up method provides an effective framework for analysing the perturbation of sharp fronts in degenerate Fisher-KPP equations, confirming the sharp-to-smooth transition mechanism as wave speed increases.

title: Numerical Solution of Pantograph Delay Integrodifferential Equation of Volterra Type: Collocation Method Based on Shifted Jacobi Polynomials
summary: Pantograph arises in electric trains, material modelling, and the modelling of quantum dot lasers. Pantograph integrodifferential equations are integrodifferential equations involving proportional delays; and they appear in fields such as electrodynamics, epidemiology, control theory, astrophysics, economics, and engineering. This research presents an efficient collocation method based on shifted Jacobi polynomials for obtaining numerical solutions of a class of first order pantograph delay integrodifferential equation of Volterra type with an initial condition. The proposed method expresses the solution of the governing equation as a shifted Jacobi polynomial series with expansion coefficients which are to be determined. Collocating at the roots of the shifted Jacobi polynomials, the underlying problem is reduced to a system of algebraic equations in the unknown expansion coefficients of the shifted Jacobi polynomial series solution. Newton's method is subsequently used to solve the resulting system of algebraic equations and numerical values of the expansion coefficients are obtained. The obtained coefficients are substituted into the assumed series solution to obtain the required numerical solutions. The applicability, reliability, efficiency, and accuracy of the shifted Jacobi collocation method are demonstrated through illustrative examples. Results obtained using the proposed method are compared with exact solutions and other published results. Comparisons of errors which are presented in tables reveal that our method approximates the solution better than the methods under comparison.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a shifted Jacobi polynomial collocation method for numerically solving first-order pantograph delay integrodifferential equations of Volterra type with initial conditions, demonstrating superior accuracy compared to existing methods through illustrative examples and error comparisons.
AI.motivation: Pantograph integrodifferential equations, which involve proportional delays, arise in diverse fields such as electrodynamics, epidemiology, control theory, astrophysics, economics, engineering, and quantum dot laser modelling. Despite their importance, efficient and accurate numerical solution methods for these equations remain a research challenge, motivating the development of a new collocation-based approach.
AI.method: The proposed method represents the solution as a shifted Jacobi polynomial series with unknown expansion coefficients. The equation is collocated at the roots of shifted Jacobi polynomials, reducing the original problem to a system of algebraic equations in the unknown coefficients. Newton's method is then applied to solve this system, after which the determined coefficients are substituted back into the series to obtain the numerical solution.
AI.result: Illustrative examples demonstrate the applicability, reliability, efficiency, and accuracy of the shifted Jacobi collocation method. Error comparisons presented in tables show that the proposed method approximates the solution more accurately than the compared existing methods.
AI.conclusion: The shifted Jacobi collocation method is an effective and superior numerical technique for solving first-order pantograph delay integrodifferential equations of Volterra type, outperforming existing methods in accuracy as evidenced by comparative error analysis.

title: A Lean Formalization of Hamilton's Three-Manifold Theorem
summary: We describe a Lean formalization of Hamilton's 1982 theorem on closed, connected three-manifolds with positive Ricci curvature. The development contains a short-time existence theorem for Ricci flow and substantial geometric-analysis infrastructure: Riemannian tensor calculus, the Levi--Civita connection, Ricci-flow evolution equations, scalar and tensor maximum principles, three-dimensional curvature algebra, preservation of Ricci pinching, and Hamilton's improved pinching estimate. The formalization follows an alternative blow-up route, rather than Hamilton's original normalized-flow proof. Its time-uniform short-time existence, maximal continuation, no-local-collapsing, and Cheeger--Gromov--Hamilton compactness pipelines have been formalized and are included in the artifact, while we give only a brief account of these companion developments and record the interfaces and consequences used by the Hamilton argument; a detailed exposition of their full constructions is deferred to the second author's forthcoming thesis. We interweave representative Lean declarations with their mathematical meaning and record the status and provenance of every major component. All source-level status claims are tied to the source release identified below.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a formalization in the Lean proof assistant of Hamilton's 1982 theorem on three-manifolds with positive Ricci curvature, including extensive geometric-analysis infrastructure such as Ricci flow, tensor calculus, maximum principles, and pinching estimates, using an alternative blow-up proof route.
AI.motivation: To formally verify a deep and important classical theorem in differential geometry — Hamilton's theorem on positive Ricci curvature in 3-manifolds — within a proof assistant, thereby demonstrating that complex geometric-analysis arguments can be mechanically checked and building reusable infrastructure for future formalization work.
AI.method: The formalization develops in Lean: (1) Riemannian tensor calculus and Levi-Civita connection infrastructure; (2) Ricci-flow evolution equations; (3) scalar and tensor maximum principles; (4) three-dimensional curvature algebra; (5) preservation of Ricci pinching and Hamilton's improved pinching estimate; and (6) an alternative blow-up route (rather than Hamilton's normalized-flow proof), supported by formalized pipelines for time-uniform short-time existence, maximal continuation, no-local-collapsing, and Cheeger-Gromov-Hamilton compactness.
AI.result: A complete Lean formalization of Hamilton's theorem, with all major components status-proven and tied to a specific source release. The companion pipelines (short-time existence, continuation, compactness) are formalized and included in the artifact, though described only at the interface level in the paper.
AI.conclusion: The work represents a major milestone in formalized mathematics, showing that a deep result in geometric analysis can be fully machine-checked, and provides substantial reusable infrastructure for future formalization efforts in differential geometry and Ricci flow.

title: Logarithmic derivatives of variational and singular stochastic partial differential equations
summary: For a stochastic partial differential equation posed on a Gelfand triple and satisfying the fully local monotone conditions of Röckner, Shang and Zhang, we compute the logarithmic derivative of the law of the solution at a fixed time along a prescribed direction of the state space. The formula is intrinsic, being expressed through the Hilbert-Schmidt Malliavin derivative $Φ_r = \mathcal{D}_r X(t)$ and the covariance $γ_t = \int_0^t Φ_r Φ_r^{*} \,\mathrm{d}r$ alone, so that neither the inversion of the first variation used in finite dimensions nor uniform Malliavin-Sobolev bounds on the Tikhonov family are called upon. It is obtained from an integration-by-parts identity on an abstract Hilbert space, a Moore-Penrose construction of a covering field on Wiener space, and a trace formula for the Tikhonov limit, specialised to the equation through the representation $Φ_r = Y(t,r)\mathcal{B}(r,X(r))$ of the Malliavin derivative by the first variation; the stochastic $p$-Laplacian and the two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equation are treated in detail. Beyond the variational class, a scalar reduction gives an integration-by-parts identity for the law of a pairing $\langle u(t),\varphi\rangle$ which passes to the renormalised limit for the singular equations of Bruned, Chandra, Chevyrev and Hairer, and which is represented by a logarithmic derivative under second-order Malliavin smoothness and negative-moment hypotheses.

AI.tldr: The paper computes the logarithmic derivative of the law of solutions to stochastic partial differential equations under fully local monotone conditions via Malliavin calculus, obtaining an intrinsic formula expressed purely through the Hilbert-Schmidt Malliavin derivative and covariance, without requiring inversion of the first variation or uniform Malliavin-Sobolev bounds. The framework extends to singular SPDEs through a scalar reduction yielding integration-by-parts identities for renormalised limits.
AI.motivation: Computing the logarithmic derivative of the law of SPDE solutions (e.g., for Wasserstein gradient flows and dimension-free Harnack inequalities) traditionally requires either finite-dimensional arguments relying on inversion of the first variation or uniform Malliavin-Sobolev bounds on Tikhonov-type regularisations, both of which are restrictive or unavailable in many settings. The paper aims to obtain such derivatives intrinsically from the Malliavin derivative and covariance alone.
AI.method: The approach combines (i) an integration-by-parts identity on an abstract Hilbert space; (ii) a Moore-Penrose construction of a covering field on Wiener space; (iii) a trace formula for the Tikhonov limit; and (iv) specialisation to the SPDE via the representation Phi_r = Y(t,r)B(r,X(r)) of the Malliavin derivative by the first variation. A scalar reduction is also developed for the law of pairings <u(t),phi> that passes to renormalised limits for singular equations.
AI.result: An intrinsic, unified formula for the logarithmic derivative is established under fully local monotone conditions, requiring neither inversion of the first variation nor uniform Malliavin-Sobolev bounds on Tikhonov families. The framework is applied to the stochastic p-Laplacian and the two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equation. For singular equations (Bruned-Chandra-Chevyrev-Hairer class), a scalar integration-by-parts identity is obtained that passes to the renormalised limit, with a logarithmic derivative representation under second-order Malliavin smoothness and negative-moment hypotheses.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a general and intrinsic method for computing logarithmic derivatives of SPDE solution laws in the fully local monotone variational framework, extends the technique to renormalised singular SPDEs, and thereby removes technical obstructions that previously required stronger regularity or dimensional assumptions.

title: Endpoint orthonormal Strichartz estimates
summary: We establish the orthonormal Strichartz estimates in the abstract Keel--Tao framework, under precisely the same hypotheses as in their original theorem. As an important consequence, we resolve the endpoint conjecture for the Schrödinger equation in dimensions $d\ge 2$, which was first raised by Frank, Lewin, Lieb, and Seiringer. This consequence also yields an affirmative answer to the conjecture for the free transport equation, which was stated in dual form by Bennett, Bez, Gutiérrez, and Lee. As a further application, we also establish a refinement of the Strichartz estimate for a single function.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes orthonormal Strichartz estimates in the abstract Keel-Tao framework under the same hypotheses as the original theorem, resolving the endpoint conjecture for the Schrödinger equation in dimensions d≥2 and the free transport equation conjecture, with applications to refined single-function Strichartz estimates.
AI.motivation: To resolve open endpoint conjectures for orthonormal Strichartz estimates in the Schrödinger equation (raised by Frank, Lewin, Lieb, and Seiringer) and the free transport equation (stated in dual form by Bennett, Bez, Gutiérrez, and Lee), by extending the abstract Keel-Tao framework to the orthonormal setting.
AI.method: The authors work within the abstract Keel-Tao framework and prove orthonormal Strichartz estimates under precisely the same hypotheses as the original Keel-Tao theorem, using the structure of the abstract dispersive framework to handle the trace-class/operator settings required for orthonormal systems.
AI.result: Resolution of the endpoint conjecture for the Schrödinger equation in d≥2, an affirmative answer to the free transport equation conjecture, and a refinement of the Strichartz estimate for a single function as a further application.
AI.conclusion: The orthonormal Strichartz estimates hold in the full generality of the Keel-Tao framework, resolving several longstanding endpoint conjectures and providing a unified abstract approach to these problems.

title: Pinchoff by surface diffusion
summary:
We construct surface diffusion flows $f:\mathbb{T}^2\times[0,T)\to\mathbb{R}^3$ that drive smooth closed embedded tori to pinchoff in finite time. The flow remains embedded for $t\in[0,T)$ and develops a curvature singularity only at a distinguished point $p$ as $t\nearrow T$. Away from $(p,T)$ the flow converges smoothly as $t\nearrow T$. We characterise the singularity profile: If $A(t)$ denotes the radius of the waist, and the surface is given locally near the waist by the rotation of a radial graph $(z,t)\mapsto r(z,t)$, then there exists a constant $μ>0$ and smooth function $U:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ such that \[
  A(t)=\{4μ(T-t)\}^{1/4}(1+o(1)),
  \qquad
  A(t)^{-1}r(A(t)ζ,t)\stackrel{C^\infty_{loc}}{\longrightarrow} U(ζ). \] Here $U$ is a rigorous realisation of the classical fundamental positive even conical similarity profile first computed numerically by Wong, Miksis, Voorhees and Davis and subsequently analysed by Bernoff, Bertozzi and Witelski.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs surface diffusion flows on embedded tori that develop finite-time pinchoff singularities, rigorously characterizing the singularity profile as a conical self-similar solution first computed numerically in prior work.
AI.motivation: To rigorously analyze and characterize the singularity formation mechanism for surface diffusion flows on tori, particularly the pinchoff phenomenon and its asymptotic profile, which had only been studied numerically before.
AI.method: The authors construct explicit surface diffusion flows on smooth closed embedded tori, analyze the flow near the singular time T, and prove that the singularity profile converges in a rescaled sense to a universal conical similarity profile U (the Wong-Miksis-Voorheis-Davis profile), with the waist radius scaling as A(t) ~ {4μ(T-t)}^(1/4).
AI.result: The flow develops a curvature singularity at a distinguished point p in finite time while remaining embedded away from that point. The rescaled singularity profile converges to the classical fundamental positive even conical similarity profile U, rigorously realizing the numerical predictions.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides the first rigorous construction and characterization of pinchoff singularities for surface diffusion flows on tori, confirming the numerically predicted self-similar conical singularity profile.

title: Two-Dimensional $β$-plane Turbulence: Dual Cascade and Zonal Jets
summary:
We derive an exact and novel expression for an averaged two-point correlation function in the statistically stationary, forced-dissipative two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations subject to the Coriolis force under the beta-plane approximation. This identity is related to the so-called geostrophic balance: it connects the effect of the Coriolis force to the pressure gradient through a two-point correlation function.
  Additionally, we provide sufficient conditions under which the asymptotics of the averaged third-order structure function at large spatial scales follow the universal third-order law of two-dimensional turbulence in the absence of the Coriolis force. This complements our previous results on small spatial scales.
  Together, our results provide a clear picture of the role of the Coriolis force in beta-plane turbulence. On the one hand, the spherically averaged rates of enstrophy and energy transfer are not affected by the Coriolis force. On the other hand, the Coriolis force contributes to anisotropic large-scale organization by altering the spatial distribution of energy and promoting the formation of zonal structures.
  The proof relies on a new formulation of the Karman-Howarth-Monin relation. For the geostrophic balance, we use a novel antisymmetric projection of the KHM relation under which only the pressure and Coriolis terms survive. For the cascade laws, we show that the Coriolis contribution to the averaged classical KHM relation vanishes identically at any scale.

AI.tldr: This paper derives an exact expression for a two-point correlation function in forced-dissipative 2D Navier-Stokes equations with beta-plane Coriolis force, linking it to geostrophic balance. It also provides sufficient conditions for the universal third-order cascade law of 2D turbulence at large scales, and shows that while the Coriolis force does not affect spherically averaged enstrophy/energy transfer rates, it drives anisotropic large-scale organization and zonal structure formation.
AI.motivation: To clarify the role of the Coriolis force in beta-plane turbulence, particularly how it affects cascade laws, geostrophic balance, and large-scale anisotropic organization in two-dimensional turbulence.
AI.method: The proof uses a new formulation of the Karman-Howarth-Monin (KHM) relation. For geostrophic balance, an antisymmetric projection of the KHM relation isolates pressure and Coriolis terms. For cascade laws, it is shown that the Coriolis contribution to the averaged classical KHM relation vanishes identically at all scales.
AI.result: An exact two-point correlation identity connecting Coriolis force to pressure gradient (geostrophic balance) is derived. Sufficient conditions are given for the universal third-order law at large scales. Results show spherically averaged enstrophy and energy transfer rates are unaffected by Coriolis force, but the force promotes anisotropic large-scale organization and zonal structure formation.
AI.conclusion: The Coriolis force does not alter isotropic energy/enstrophy cascade rates but contributes to anisotropic organization at large scales by modifying energy spatial distribution and promoting zonal structure formation, providing a comprehensive picture of Coriolis effects in beta-plane turbulence.

title: Boundary-weighted barycenter spaces
summary: We study boundary-weighted barycenter spaces, in which an interior support point has cost (or weight) two and a boundary support point has cost one. These spaces are finite-dimensional topological models for the concentration patterns produced by noncompact boundary Euler--Lagrange functionals: an interior bubble carries twice the quantized mass of a boundary bubble, and very negative sublevels are therefore modeled by boundary-weighted rather than ordinary barycenters. The paper gives a systematic algebraic-topological treatment of these spaces. We construct the mixed strata, the closed-stratum poset, and the triangular boundary-weighted colimit filtration; compute the Euler characteristic; and prove a homology decomposition in terms of ordinary barycenter spaces of \(\partial M\) and \(M/\partial M\). We then specialize the formulas to compact connected orientable surfaces with boundary and to hemispheres, obtaining explicit rational Betti polynomials and, for surfaces, the mod-two polynomials required by the mean-field application. Finally, we explain how these polynomials measure the topology at infinity in the resonant Neumann mean-field equation on a compact surface with boundary.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a systematic algebraic-topological study of boundary-weighted barycenter spaces—finite-dimensional models for concentration patterns in noncompact boundary Euler-Lagrange functionals, where interior bubbles carry twice the mass of boundary bubbles. The authors construct mixed strata, closed-stratum posets, and triangular boundary-weighted colimit filtrations; compute Euler characteristics; prove homology decompositions in terms of ordinary barycenter spaces; and specialize to explicit rational Betti polynomials for surfaces and hemispheres, with applications to the resonant Neumann mean-field equation.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses the need for accurate topological models of concentration patterns in noncompact boundary Euler-Lagrange functionals. Standard barycenter spaces fail to capture the asymmetry where interior bubbles have twice the quantized mass of boundary bubbles, motivating the introduction of boundary-weighted barycenter spaces as more faithful finite-dimensional models.
AI.method: The authors develop a systematic algebraic-topological framework for boundary-weighted barycenter spaces, including construction of mixed strata, the closed-stratum poset, and a triangular boundary-weighted colimit filtration. They compute Euler characteristics and prove a homology decomposition relating these spaces to ordinary barycenter spaces of the boundary and the quotient manifold. The general formulas are then specialized to orientable surfaces with boundary and hemispheres to obtain explicit Betti polynomials (rational and mod-two).
AI.result: The paper yields explicit Euler characteristics and homology decompositions for boundary-weighted barycenter spaces, along with concrete rational Betti polynomials for compact connected orientable surfaces with boundary and for hemispheres. It also provides the mod-two polynomials required for the mean-field application, demonstrating how these topological quantities measure the topology at infinity in the resonant Neumann mean-field equation.
AI.conclusion: The boundary-weighted barycenter spaces provide the correct finite-dimensional topological framework for modelling concentration patterns in noncompact boundary Euler-Lagrange functionals. The computed Betti polynomials encode topology at infinity for the resonant Neumann mean-field equation on compact surfaces with boundary, establishing a direct link between algebraic topology and PDE analysis.

title: Componentwise Geometry and Monodromy of Generalized Lamé Equations
summary:
We develop a componentwise geometric and monodromy theory for the generalized Lamé equation on an elliptic curve with singularities at $0$ and $\pm p$. Its log-free locus decomposes canonically into two irreducible components, corresponding to the even and non-even symmetries of the potential.
  Building on the spectral theory of the even component, we construct the hyperelliptic spectral curve, Baker--Akhiezer functions, and addition map of the non-even component, and prove that \[
  \degσ_{n,p}^{(1)}=n(n+1).
  \]
  After quotienting by the involution $T\mapsto -T$, we show that the non-even spectral curve is naturally isomorphic to the classical Lamé spectral curve, compatibly with the addition map and the rational function $κ$. Consequently, every non-even generalized Lamé equation is monodromy equivalent to a unique classical Lamé equation on the same elliptic curve, via the explicit correspondence \[ \widetilde B=T^2-n(n+1)\wp(p). \]
  Fixing $\widetilde B$ yields an isomonodromic family as $p$ varies. The correspondence transfers the spectral geometry, finite-gap structure, and finite-monodromy theories, together with the curvature equations on flat tori, to the non-even component. Combining with the Painlevé VI deformation of the even component, we give a componentwise interpretation of the generalized Lamé degeneration.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a complete componentwise geometric and monodromy theory for the generalized Lamé equation on an elliptic curve, decomposing its log-free locus into even and non-even irreducible components. For the non-even component, the authors construct the hyperelliptic spectral curve, Baker–Akhiezer functions, and addition map, prove deg σ = n(n+1), and show that after quotienting by T ↦ -T the spectral curve is isomorphic to the classical Lamé spectral curve. This yields an explicit monodromy equivalence between non-even generalized Lamé and classical Lamé equations via B̃ = T² - n(n+1)℘(p), transferring spectral geometry, finite-gap structure, and finite-monodromy theories, and enabling an isomonodromic family and componentwise interpretation of the generalized Lamé degeneration.
AI.motivation: To provide a complete geometric and monodromy theory for the generalized Lamé equation (with singularities at 0 and ±p) by decomposing its parameter space into irreducible components and establishing connections to the classical Lamé spectral theory, thereby unifying and transferring spectral, monodromy, and geometric results.
AI.method: The paper decomposes the log-free locus into even and non-even irreducible components based on potential symmetries. For the non-even component, it constructs a hyperelliptic spectral curve, Baker–Akhiezer functions, and addition map, proving a degree formula. It then quotients by the involution T ↦ -T to obtain a natural isomorphism with the classical Lamé spectral curve, yielding an explicit correspondence B̃ = T² - n(n+1)℘(p) between the non-even generalized Lamé and classical Lamé equations.
AI.result: The paper proves deg σ_{n,p}^{(1)} = n(n+1), establishes a natural isomorphism between the non-even spectral curve (after T ↦ -T quotient) and the classical Lamé spectral curve, and shows that every non-even generalized Lamé equation is monodromy equivalent to a unique classical Lamé equation on the same elliptic curve. Fixing B̃ produces an isomonodromic family as p varies.
AI.conclusion: The correspondence transfers spectral geometry, finite-gap structure, finite-monodromy theories, and curvature equations on flat tori to the non-even component. Combined with the Painlevé VI deformation of the even component, this gives a complete componentwise interpretation of the generalized Lamé degeneration.

title: A criterion on weak type $(1,1)$ bound of rough singular integrals
summary: In this paper we establish a criterion on weak type $(1,\,1)$ bound of the following rough singular integral $$T_{Ω,K,a}f(x)={\rm p.v.}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}Ω(x-y)K(x,y)m_{x,y}a f(y)dy,$$ where $m_{x,y}a=\int_0^1a(sx+(1-s)y)ds$ with $a\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $\hat{a}\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$, $Ω$ is homogeneous of degree zero, integrable in $\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ and satisfies the cancellation condition $\int_{\mathbb{S}^{n-1}}Ω(θ)dσ(θ)=0$ and $K$ is a measurable function defined on $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n\setminus \{(x,x):x\in\mathbb{R}^n\}$ and satisfies a Hölder condition. By assuming that $Ω\in L\log L(\mathbb{S}^{n-1})$ and the operator $T_{Ω, K}f(x)={\rm p.v.}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}Ω(x-y)K(x,y)f(y)dy$ is bounded on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$, we prove the weak type (1,1) bound of $T_{Ω,K,a}$. As several applications, we obtain a large class of singular integral operators which possess weak type $(1,\,1)$ bound. The main results of this paper essentially extend and generalize some known ones.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a criterion for the weak type (1,1) boundedness of a rough singular integral operator with a variable coefficient kernel. Under the assumptions of cancellation, L log L integrability of the angular part, and L² boundedness, the author proves the weak (1,1) estimate and extends several known results as applications.
AI.motivation: The study aims to extend existing results on weak type (1,1) estimates for singular integral operators by incorporating a more general setup with a variable Hölder-continuous kernel K(x,y), an L log L angular integrability condition, and an additional averaging factor m_{x,y}a. This generalizes prior work and provides a broad criterion applicable to many classes of operators.
AI.method: The proof assumes Ω is homogeneous of degree zero with cancellation on the sphere, Ω ∈ L log L(S^{n-1}), and that the associated operator T_{Ω,K} is L²-bounded. Under these conditions and a Hölder condition on K, the author establishes the weak (1,1) bound for the modified operator with the extra averaging term m_{x,y}a.
AI.result: A criterion for weak type (1,1) boundedness of the rough singular integral operator T_{Ω,K,a} is proved. This yields a large class of singular integral operators with weak (1,1) bounds as applications.
AI.conclusion: The main results substantially extend and generalize known results on weak type (1,1) estimates for rough singular integrals, broadening the applicable class of operators and kernel conditions.

title: Uniqueness of capillary Gauss solitons
summary: We prove the rigidity conjecture of [14, Conjecture 1.2] for smooth strictly convex capillary Gauss solitons in a Euclidean half-space with an acute contact angle: every such soliton is a spherical cap. Combined with our previous convergence result for the capillary Gauss curvature flow [14, Theorem 1.1], it follows that the flow starting from a strictly convex capillary hypersurface with an acute contact angle converges to a capillary spherical cap, after a suitable rescaling.

AI.tldr: The paper proves the rigidity conjecture for smooth strictly convex capillary Gauss solitons in a Euclidean half-space with an acute contact angle, showing all such solitons are spherical caps. Combined with prior convergence results, this implies the capillary Gauss curvature flow converges to a capillary spherical cap after rescaling.
AI.motivation: To resolve the rigidity conjecture (Conjecture 1.2 from [14]) which asks whether capillary Gauss solitons in a Euclidean half-space with acute contact angle must be spherical caps. This is a fundamental classification question for solitons that arise in the study of capillary Gauss curvature flow.
AI.method: The paper proves the rigidity conjecture for smooth strictly convex capillary Gauss solitons in a Euclidean half-space with an acute contact angle, establishing that every such soliton must be a spherical cap.
AI.result: The rigidity conjecture is proven: every smooth strictly convex capillary Gauss soliton in a Euclidean half-space with an acute contact angle is a spherical cap.
AI.conclusion: Combined with the previous convergence result (Theorem 1.1 in [14]), the capillary Gauss curvature flow starting from a strictly convex capillary hypersurface with an acute contact angle converges to a capillary spherical cap after suitable rescaling, giving a complete convergence picture for the flow.

title: Fractality of the Schrödinger Density for Rough Data
summary: The observable of the Talbot effect is the intensity behind the grating: the density of the evolving field, not the field itself. Its fractality was previously known only for step data with rational jumps. We prove the general case. For arbitrary real data of bounded variation with at least one jump, the density of the free Schrödinger evolution on the torus is fractal at almost every time, with graph of upper box dimension exactly three halves. Its critical Sobolev mass diverges logarithmically, at a rate given in closed form by Wiener's jump statistic of the datum and independent of the positions and phases of the jumps. The same rate is halved along time traces and doubled for the Airy flow, so the critical mass probes the dispersion relation. Transported by the rank calculus of derangetropy operators, the theory equips every probability law with a quantum carpet: Gauss-sum revivals on quantile cells at rational times, a universal fractal at almost every other. The spectral growth rate of a single measured intensity profile returns the jump content of the grating, a prediction open to test in optical and matter-wave interferometry.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that the density of the free Schrödinger evolution on the torus is fractal for arbitrary real data of bounded variation with at least one jump, at almost every time, with upper box dimension exactly 3/2. The critical Sobolev mass diverges logarithmically at a rate given by Wiener's jump statistic, which is halved along time traces and doubled for Airy flow. The theory provides a universal quantum carpet for every probability law and offers testable predictions for optical and matter-wave interferometry.
AI.motivation: The Talbot effect's observable is intensity (density), not the field itself. Fractality of this density was previously only known for step data with rational jumps; the general case remained open. Understanding the general case is important both theoretically and experimentally for interferometry.
AI.method: The proof generalizes beyond rational jumps to arbitrary real data of bounded variation. The framework uses the rank calculus of derangetropy operators, which transports the theory and equips probability laws with quantum carpets—Gauss-sum revivals on quantile cells at rational times and universal fractality at almost every other time.
AI.result: For arbitrary real bounded-variation data with at least one jump, the density is fractal at almost every time with upper box dimension exactly 3/2. The critical Sobolev mass diverges logarithmically at a closed-form rate given by Wiener's jump statistic (independent of jump positions and phases). The rate is halved along time traces and doubled for Airy flow. The spectral growth rate of a single intensity profile recovers the jump content of the grating.
AI.conclusion: The critical Sobolev mass probes the dispersion relation (via halving/doubling along different flows), and the theory yields experimentally testable predictions in optical and matter-wave interferometry by reading the jump content from a single intensity profile.

title: Unique continuation for $\bar\partial u = Vu$ at infinity
summary: Motivated by Landis's conjecture on unique continuation at infinity for the Laplacian, we study the corresponding property for the Cauchy-Riemann operator. We prove that every weak solution of $\bar\partial u=Vu$ on a neighborhood of infinity, with $V\in L^\infty$, vanishes identically if it decays exponentially at a rate greater than $ 2\|V\|_{L^\infty}$. This conclusion is sharp both in the constant $2\|V\|_{L^\infty}$ and in the order of exponential decay required. More generally, we establish unique continuation at infinity for a broad class of radially decaying bounded potentials, with optimal decay rates determined by the decay of the potential. We also obtain related unique continuation results for $L^2$ potentials and for compactly supported potentials under weaker assumptions at infinity.

AI.tldr: This paper proves unique continuation at infinity for the Cauchy-Riemann operator, showing that weak solutions of ∂̄u = Vu that decay exponentially faster than a sharp threshold (2‖V‖L∞) must vanish identically, with optimal constants and generalizations to radially decaying and L² potentials.
AI.motivation: The work is motivated by Landis's conjecture on unique continuation at infinity for the Laplacian, and the authors seek to study the analogous property for the Cauchy-Riemann (∂̄) operator, which has not been previously established in this context.
AI.method: The authors employ analytic techniques to prove unique continuation at infinity for weak solutions of ∂̄u = Vu with bounded potentials V ∈ L∞, establishing sharp decay thresholds. They extend the results to a broader class of radially decaying potentials and L² potentials, deriving optimal decay rates tied to the potential's decay profile.
AI.result: The paper proves that any weak solution decaying exponentially faster than 2‖V‖L∞ must vanish identically, with this threshold proven sharp both in the constant and decay order. Generalizations include optimal decay rates for radially decaying potentials and results for L² and compactly supported potentials under weaker assumptions.
AI.conclusion: The authors establish a sharp, optimal unique continuation at infinity theorem for the Cauchy-Riemann operator analogous to Landis's conjecture for the Laplacian, with results covering various classes of potentials and decay conditions.

title: Bifurcation structure and mesa pattern formation in a one-component nonlocal adhesion model with population pressure and degenerate mobility
summary: We analyze pattern formation from a homogeneous steady state in a one-component nonlocal adhesion model with population pressure and degenerate mobility. First, using linear stability analysis, we derive the instability threshold and a selection rule for the fastest-growing mode, and elucidate the mechanism by which the selected wavenumber shifts toward lower wavenumbers as the mean density increases. We then perform a weakly nonlinear analysis near the critical adhesion strength and derive an explicit expression for the Landau coefficient in the Stuart--Landau equation. This expression shows that the critical bifurcation is classified as supercritical or subcritical according to the mean density, the nonlinear exponent, and the second-harmonic response ratio of the kernel. Furthermore, we show that a large nonlinear exponent promotes a transition to subcriticality and confirm, through numerical bifurcation analysis and time-dependent simulations, a bifurcation structure with a fold point and the formation of mesa patterns. Finally, through the energy limit as \(m\to\infty\), we relate the observed mesa profiles to a capacity-constrained limiting structure.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes pattern formation in a one-component nonlocal adhesion model with population pressure and degenerate mobility, deriving instability thresholds via linear stability analysis, classifying bifurcation type (supercritical/subcritical) via weakly nonlinear analysis with an explicit Landau coefficient, and relating mesa pattern formation at large nonlinear exponents to a capacity-constrained limiting structure.
AI.motivation: To understand how nonlocal adhesion, population pressure, and degenerate mobility interact to drive pattern formation, and to characterize how the bifurcation type and pattern selection depend on system parameters such as mean density and nonlinear exponent.
AI.method: The authors use three analytical/numerical approaches: (1) linear stability analysis to derive the instability threshold and fastest-growing mode selection rule; (2) weakly nonlinear analysis near critical adhesion strength to derive the Landau coefficient in the Stuart–Landau equation, determining whether the bifurcation is supercritical or subcritical; and (3) numerical bifurcation analysis, time-dependent simulations, and an energy limit as m→∞ to study mesa pattern formation and its relation to a capacity-constrained limiting structure.
AI.result: The analysis shows that the selected wavenumber shifts toward lower values as mean density increases. The Landau coefficient reveals that the bifurcation can be supercritical or subcritical depending on mean density, nonlinear exponent, and kernel second-harmonic response. A large nonlinear exponent promotes subcriticality, leading to a fold point in the bifurcation structure and the formation of mesa patterns. The m→∞ energy limit connects mesa profiles to a capacity-constrained limiting structure.
AI.conclusion: The model exhibits rich bifurcation behavior where the nonlinear exponent plays a critical role in determining whether pattern formation is supercritical or subcritical, with subcritical transitions producing mesa patterns that can be interpreted through a capacity-constrained energy limit.

title: Monotonicity Principle and "p-Laplace Signature" for Tomography in Nonlinear Elliptic Inverse Problems
summary:
This paper proposes a framework for treating the inverse obstacle problem for nonlinear elliptic equations with nonlinear materials.
  The problem is challenging because nonlinear materials exhibit a rich diversity of scenarios to consider, since nonlinearity can take different forms. In this article, after categorizing the nonlinearities into a few fundamental classes, a dedicated imaging method is proposed for each class, derived by combining two powerful concepts: the Monotonicity Principle (MP) and the $p-$Laplace Signature (pLS).
  The Monotonicity Principle (MP), recently extended to nonlinear materials, provides a monotonic relationship between the material property and the measured quantity (the Average Dirichlet-to-Neumann map) that can be \lq\lq inverted\rq\rq \ to find the shape of anomalies.
  The $p-$Laplace Signature (pLS) allows for modelling the solution of an elliptic PDE with nonlinear materials, for large or small boundary data, in terms of a proper $p-$Laplace equation that captures the essence (the signature) of the problem. For example, pLS with $p=2$ allows the reduction of a nonlinear elliptic PDE to a linear one, providing a powerful bridge for applying imaging methods and algorithms developed for linear materials.
  In this contribution, the two pillars of MP and pLS are combined in new imaging methods to enlarge the class of nonlinearity that can be treated within the inverse obstacle problem. Moreover, the theoretical limits of the methods are provided in the ideal case of noise-free measurements: outer-support reconstruction when $p=2$, and convex-hull reconstruction when $p\neq2$.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a framework for the inverse obstacle problem in nonlinear elliptic equations by combining the Monotonicity Principle (MP) and the p-Laplace Signature (pLS) to develop imaging methods for different classes of nonlinearities.
AI.motivation: Nonlinear materials exhibit diverse scenarios with different forms of nonlinearity, making the inverse obstacle problem challenging. The authors aim to enlarge the class of nonlinearity that can be treated within this problem.
AI.method: The paper categorizes nonlinearities into fundamental classes and proposes a dedicated imaging method for each class by combining two concepts: (1) the Monotonicity Principle (MP), which provides a monotonic relationship between material properties and the Average Dirichlet-to-Neumann map; and (2) the p-Laplace Signature (pLS), which models the solution in terms of a p-Laplace equation capturing the essence of the problem.
AI.result: The methods achieve theoretical limits in the ideal case of noise-free measurements: outer-support reconstruction when p=2 (where nonlinear PDEs reduce to linear ones), and convex-hull reconstruction when p≠2.
AI.conclusion: By combining MP and pLS, the proposed framework broadens the range of treatable nonlinearities in inverse obstacle problems, with rigorous theoretical guarantees on reconstruction limits.

title: Semilinear overdetermined problems, a divergence formula, and geometric inequalities
summary: Considering an $n$-dimensional compact Riemannian manifold with a boundary that satisfies a Serrin-type problem, we prove sharp upper and lower bounds for the area of such a boundary. Then, we present the main result of this paper: a divergence formula for a special vector field on a given Riemannian manifold. This divergence formula is closely related to sub-static manifolds and related metrics, e.g., $V$-static, static, and electrostatic manifolds. We show Minkowski-type inequalities for $V$-sub-static manifolds under different Neumann boundary conditions. Moreover, we prove an area-charge inequality for compact (and noncompact) electrostatic manifolds. The main application of the divergence formula presented in this work generalizes the classical result of Boucher--Gibbons--Horowitz: we prove that an asymptotically hyperbolic space of a static spacetime satisfying the null convergence condition must be the hyperbolic space.

AI.tldr: This paper derives sharp area bounds for boundaries of compact Riemannian manifolds satisfying a Serrin-type problem, establishes a key divergence formula applicable to sub-static, V-static, static, and electrostatic manifolds, proves Minkowski-type inequalities under Neumann boundary conditions, and generalizes the Boucher–Gibbons–Horowitz result by showing asymptotically hyperbolic static spacetimes satisfying the null convergence condition must be hyperbolic space.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to deepen the geometric and analytic understanding of sub-static manifolds and their boundary behavior. It seeks to unify and generalize existing results in static spacetime geometry—particularly the classical Boucher–Gibbons–Horowitz theorem—through a novel divergence formula and to establish sharp geometric inequalities connecting area, charge, and mass in electrostatic and V-static settings.
AI.method: The approach involves: (1) analyzing Serrin-type boundary value problems on compact Riemannian manifolds to obtain sharp area bounds; (2) constructing a special vector field on the manifold and proving a divergence formula for it; (3) applying this formula under various Neumann boundary conditions to derive Minkowski-type inequalities for V-sub-static manifolds; (4) proving area-charge inequalities for both compact and noncompact electrostatic manifolds; and (5) using the divergence formula to prove rigidity of asymptotically hyperbolic spaces in static spacetimes under the null convergence condition.
AI.result: The paper obtains sharp upper and lower area bounds for Serrin-type boundaries, establishes Minkowski-type inequalities for V-sub-static manifolds, proves area-charge inequalities for electrostatic manifolds (compact and noncompact), and generalizes the Boucher–Gibbons–Horowitz theorem by showing that any asymptotically hyperbolic static spacetime satisfying the null convergence condition must be the hyperbolic space.
AI.conclusion: The divergence formula serves as a powerful unifying tool that recovers and extends classical rigidity and inequality results across several related classes of manifolds (static, V-static, electrostatic, and sub-static), culminating in a full rigidity statement for asymptotically hyperbolic spaces.

title: Big Pieces of Regular Parabolic (bi-)Lipschitz Images is Equivalent to Parabolic Uniform Rectifiability
summary:
We define the notion of regular parabolic (bi-)Lipschitz images as the parabolic (bi-)Lipschitz maps from $n$-dimensional space time which, up to translation, fix the $t$ variable and whose spatial components are each regular parabolic Lipschitz functions. We show that any parabolic Ahlfors-David regular is parabolic uniformly rectifiable if and only if it has big pieces of parabolic Lipschitz images of $n$-dimensional space time if and only if it has big pieces of parabolic bi-Lipschitz images of $n$-dimensional space time. This further extends the David-Semmes theory to the parabolic setting.
  Our proof combines the ideas of the first authors previous work [BH12,BHH+22] and some ideas of Azzam and Schul [AS12]. The proof easily adapts (and is far less complicated) to the Euclidean case to give an alternative proof of the analogous fact.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the David-Semmes theory to the parabolic setting by proving that an n-dimensional parabolic Ahlfors-David regular set is parabolically uniformly rectifiable if and only if it has big pieces of parabolic Lipschitz images of n-dimensional spacetime, if and only if it has big pieces of parabolic bi-Lipschitz images. The proof combines ideas from prior work by the first author and Azzam-Schul, and also provides a simplified alternative proof in the Euclidean case.
AI.motivation: The goal is to extend the classical David-Semmes theory of uniform rectifiability from the Euclidean setting to the parabolic setting by characterizing parabolic uniformly rectifiable sets in terms of big pieces of Lipschitz and bi-Lipschitz images of n-dimensional spacetime.
AI.method: The authors define regular parabolic (bi-)Lipschitz images as parabolic (bi-)Lipschitz maps from n-dimensional spacetime that fix the time variable up to translation, with spatial components being regular parabolic Lipschitz functions. They then prove equivalences between parabolic uniform rectifiability, having big pieces of parabolic Lipschitz images, and having big pieces of parabolic bi-Lipschitz images. The proof combines ideas from prior work (BH12, BHH+22) and Azzam-Schul (AS12).
AI.result: The main result establishes that for parabolic Ahlfors-David regular sets, parabolic uniform rectifiability is equivalent to having big pieces of parabolic Lipschitz images of n-dimensional spacetime, which is also equivalent to having big pieces of parabolic bi-Lipschitz images. Additionally, the proof adapts to the Euclidean case with less complexity, giving an alternative proof of the analogous Euclidean result.
AI.conclusion: The paper successfully extends the David-Semmes theory to the parabolic setting, establishing characterizations of parabolic uniform rectifiability via big pieces of Lipschitz and bi-Lipschitz images. The Euclidean case is recovered as a simpler corollary of the proof technique.

title: Distribution of zeros of holomorphic functions and resonances in logarithmic regions for Schroedinger operators on Euclidean space
summary: Motivated by scattering theory, this paper proves general results about the distribution of zeros in logarithmic neighborhoods of the real axis for a certain class of functions holomorphic in the closed lower half-plane. We define a new \emph{indicator function} that measures the growth of the holomorphic function along logarithmic curves, and connect this to the distribution of zeros of the function. This is related to classical results on the distribution of zeros in sectors for entire functions of completely regular growth. These results can be applied to the determinant of the scattering matrix of a Schrodinger operator on odd-dimensional Euclidean space, yielding bounds on resonance counting functions for logarithmic neighborhoods of the real axis. As a further application, we study a certain family of potentials in one dimension having jump-like singularities. Using our complex-analytic results we show that the singularities can lead to many -- and even infinitely many -- strings of resonances along logarithmic curves. We connect the properties of these strings of resonances, including their location and linear density, both to the parameters describing the singularities of the potential and to the asymptotic behavior of the scattering determinant.

AI.tldr: This paper develops complex-analytic results on the distribution of zeros in logarithmic neighborhoods of the real axis for functions holomorphic in the closed lower half-plane, motivated by scattering theory. A new indicator function measuring growth along logarithmic curves is introduced and connected to zero distributions. These results are applied to scattering matrix determinants for Schrödinger operators and to one-dimensional potentials with jump-like singularities, revealing resonance strings along logarithmic curves.
AI.motivation: The paper is motivated by scattering theory and aims to generalize classical results on zero distribution in sectors (for entire functions of completely regular growth) to the setting of zeros in logarithmic neighborhoods of the real axis for functions holomorphic in the closed lower half-plane.
AI.method: The authors define a new indicator function that measures growth of a holomorphic function along logarithmic curves, and connect this indicator to the distribution of zeros. This provides a general complex-analytic framework that is then applied to scattering determinants of Schrödinger operators on odd-dimensional Euclidean space and to one-dimensional potentials with jump-like singularities.
AI.result: The results yield bounds on resonance counting functions for logarithmic neighborhoods of the real axis in the odd-dimensional Schrödinger operator setting. For one-dimensional potentials with jump-like singularities, the paper shows that singularities can produce many—or even infinitely many—strings of resonances along logarithmic curves, with their location and linear density connected to singularity parameters and scattering determinant asymptotics.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes a new general framework for studying zero distributions in logarithmic neighborhoods, with concrete applications to scattering theory that reveal previously unknown resonance structure for potentials with singularities.

title: Instantons in a Double-Well are Poisson Distributed
summary:
We give a rigorous realization of the dilute instanton picture for a semiclassical Schrödinger operator with a symmetric double-well potential on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Using a localized Feynman--Kac representation, we decompose the heat-kernel trace according to the number of passages made by a Brownian bridge between shrinking neighborhoods of the two wells. We identify the weight of one passage with a hopping coefficient $ρ_λ$,
  $\displaystyle ρ_λ=
\int_{\partialΩ} \left( \nabla\overline{\varphi_{λ,0}^Ω}\, \varphi_{λ,0}^{-Ω} -
\overline{\varphi_{λ,0}^Ω}\, \nabla\varphi_{λ,0}^{-Ω} \right)\cdotν. $

title: Scalar charge bounds for extremal black hole formation
summary:
I prove that a collapsing charged scalar field with scalar charge $\mathfrak{e}$ that forms an exactly extremal Reissner--Nordström black hole à la Kehle--Unger with radius $r_+$ must satisfy $|\mathfrak{e}|r_+ > \frac{1}{3}$. In contrast, I also show that no such bound exists for subextremal collapse: a scalar field with an arbitrary $\mathfrak{e} \ne 0$ can form a subextremal black hole with an arbitrary (subextremal) charge-to-mass ratio.
  Complementing the extremal bound, I prove that a Schwarzschild black hole can become extremal if $|\mathfrak{e}|r_+ > \sqrt{\frac{3 + \sqrt{33}}{3}}$. The fact that $|\mathfrak{e}|r_+$ can be taken to be of order unity could be considered evidence that the third law of black hole mechanics in vacuum is false.

AI.tldr: This paper proves a bound on the scalar charge-to-radius ratio for extremal Reissner-Nordström black hole formation via collapsing charged scalar fields, showing |e|r₊ > 1/3 for exactly extremal collapse, while demonstrating no such bound exists for subextremal collapse. It also shows Schwarzschild black holes can become extremal when |e|r₊ > √((3+√33)/3).
AI.motivation: To understand the constraints on scalar field parameters required for forming extremal vs. subextremal charged black holes, and to investigate whether the third law of black hole mechanics (which states extremal black holes cannot form via continuous physical processes) holds or fails.
AI.method: Analytical proofs establishing inequalities on the scalar charge-to-radius ratio for extremal Reissner-Nordström black hole formation, following the Kehle-Unger collapse construction framework, with complementary analysis of the subextremal case showing arbitrary charge-to-mass ratios are achievable.
AI.result: For exactly extremal Reissner-Nordström collapse, the scalar field must satisfy |e|r₊ > 1/3. For subextremal collapse, arbitrary scalar charge is permitted with arbitrary subextremal charge-to-mass ratios. For extremalization of Schwarzschild black holes, the bound is |e|r₊ > √((3+√33)/3).
AI.conclusion: Since the scalar charge-to-radius ratios involved are of order unity (not requiring exotic parameter regimes), this suggests that extremal black hole formation is physically realizable, providing evidence that the third law of black hole mechanics may be false in vacuum.

title: A Stochastic Flow for the Stochastic Allen-Cahn Equation with Multiplicative Noise

AI.tldr: The paper establishes the existence of a stochastic flow on L^∞(T) for the stochastic Allen-Cahn equation with multiplicative noise using regularity structures, and shows the flow is differentiable with respect to initial conditions under additional smoothness assumptions on the noise coefficient.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to prove pathwise well-posedness and differentiability of solution flows for singular stochastic PDEs like the stochastic Allen-Cahn equation with multiplicative space-time white noise, where classical solution theories fail due to the roughness of the noise.
AI.method: The strategy employs regularity structures to obtain pathwise a priori estimates. The paper considers a general singular multiplicative equation with superlinear damping driven by noises of parabolic regularity α-2 for α∈(0,1), which is lifted to a weakly admissible model. Uniform estimates are shown to hold under a condition relating the damping exponent m to the noise regularity α.
AI.result: The required estimates hold whenever m > (2-α)/α · ε_α, where ε_α = 1 - α(1 - 2/(3-α)) ∈ (0,1). This shows the strength of the damping only needs to depend on the regularity of the driving noise. Under additional smoothness of σ, the stochastic flow is shown to be differentiable with respect to its initial condition.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes existence of solution flows for the stochastic Allen-Cahn equation on the torus in the space of bounded functions, with a damping condition determined purely by noise regularity, and proves differentiability of the flow under smooth noise coefficients.
